target.title: feat(sessions): create concise titles for saved sessions
target.body:
Closes #77165
Related #89705

## What Problem This Solves

Users with many saved sessions only had manual names, first-message fallbacks, or session-id fallbacks, so session history was hard to scan and search.

This PR adds an opt-in path that stores a durable `autoTitle` once enough direct user turns exist, while keeping manual labels/display names/origin labels/subjects higher priority.

The intended result is that enabled sessions can show and search concise stored titles in the gateway and Control UI, without changing default behavior or requiring a migration/backfill.

Out of scope: manual rename UI, migration/backfill for existing sessions, default-enabling generated titles, provider/channel/plugin capability changes, agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior, ConfigIO typing, generic session-store merge policy, and test-project routing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The feature is implemented as a default-off `sessionTitle` config surface plus additive `autoTitle` session metadata. The background title task reads only direct user text from the transcript head, skips heartbeat, internal-system, and inter-session/tool-mediated provenance, ignores textless/media-only records, caps each message and the total model input, and writes only if the persisted `sessionId` still matches.

The title lifecycle is kept at the session metadata source of truth: `autoTitle` is created once after a successful reply, persisted without refreshing `updatedAt`, cleared on reset/new/rollover, and projected to gateway and Control UI consumers. This avoids recomputing titles in display fallbacks and avoids making an older session look newly active when a delayed title write lands later.

Manual title sources remain authoritative, and the feature stays opt-in/default-off. The remaining product/privacy/auth-profile routing decisions are maintainer-owned because enabled sessions send bounded transcript excerpts to the selected title model.

## User Impact

When `sessionTitle.enabled` is true, users with many saved sessions can identify conversations by concise stored titles instead of first-message snippets or ids.

Default-off behavior is unchanged. Existing manual names still win over generated titles, reset/rollover clears generated metadata without removing manual names, and late background title writes do not reorder sessions by refreshing activity timestamps.

## Evidence

- **Fix classification:** Root-cause feature completion for opt-in model-created session titles.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the scoped code update after focused validation and local real gateway proof; maintainer product/privacy/auth acceptance remains maintainer-owned before merge.
- **Root cause:** Saved sessions had no durable generated-title source of truth, so session lists fell back to manual names, first user message snippets, or session ids.
- **CI repair root cause:** The native TypeScript preview check lost narrowing through the direct-user-message boolean helper, so the helper is now a type predicate without changing runtime behavior.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** `autoTitle` is created once in the reply lifecycle, stored on the session entry, preserved without refreshing session activity, cleared with reset/rollover state, and projected to gateway/Control UI instead of being recomputed by display fallbacks.
- **Patch quality notes:** The broad catches are intentional isolation for a non-blocking background title task; failures log or no-op instead of interrupting the user reply. The `null`/`false` returns are explicit skip/no-title states for invalid, absent, stale, manually titled, or unreadable sessions.
- **What did NOT change:** No unrelated behavior, no default enablement, no migration/backfill, no manual rename UI, no channel/provider/plugin capability change, no agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior change, and no ConfigIO or generic session-store merge policy change.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `autoTitle` is persisted as session metadata and projected outward; gateway and UI do not maintain a second title source. Runtime auth selection for this path is kept behind internal runtime code so the public runtime-auth helper contract is not expanded.
- **Related open PR / same-contract scan:** Related context is tracked in #89705. This update is scoped to the existing PR branch for #77165 and does not open a competing new PR or broaden the public provider-auth helper contract.
- **Target test file:** `src/auto-reply/reply/session-title-generator.test.ts`, `src/commands/sessions.test.ts`, `src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server.sessions.list-changed.test.ts`, and focused Control UI session tests.
- **Scenario locked in:** Enabled sessions with enough direct user turns get one bounded stored title; manual titles and stale async writes prevent overwrite; reset/new/rollover clears generated titles while preserving manual display names and session activity ordering.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The feature spans title creation, persistence, reset/rollover cleanup, gateway projection, and UI projection; the final diff removes earlier nonessential `sessions_list`, ConfigIO, generic store merge, test-routing, and public helper expansion work.
- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility, session-state, public config/schema, auth-provider routing, availability, privacy/cost boundary.
- **Risk explanation:** The highest-risk area is sending bounded transcript excerpts to the title model when the feature is explicitly enabled.
- **Why acceptable:** The feature is opt-in/default-off, filters non-direct, internal-system, and non-text user records, caps input size, skips manual-title sessions, guards stale writes by `sessionId`, writes `autoTitle` without refreshing `updatedAt`, and runs after reply delivery.
- **Main sync state:** The branch was synced with current `origin/main`; the `session-utils` conflict preserved both the new label-priority behavior from main and the generated `autoTitle` behavior from this PR. target.title: fix(update): warn about stale gateway when restart is skipped after version change
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale-gateway warning visibility for readers of issue #92241.

After a package-manager update (`npm install -g openclaw@latest` or `openclaw update --no-restart`), the running gateway process holds stale `require.cache` entries. Inbound messages can hit `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and be silently dropped while the gateway appears healthy.

`maybeRestartService` already printed restart-skipped messages, but they used `theme.muted` (dimmed/gray text) that was easy to miss in terminal output.

## Why This Change Was Made

Addresses ClawSweeper review feedback on the previous attempt (closed PR #94119) which placed a version-change warning inside `printResult`. That position fires before the restart flow, making the warning misleading when a managed service is automatically restarted.

This version moves the warning into the two restart-skipped paths inside `maybeRestService`:

1. **--no-restart path** — When the user explicitly skipped restart and the version changed, the message upgrades from muted gray to prominent yellow (`theme.warn`) and references issue #92241.
2. **No installed service path** — When no managed gateway service is found and the version changed, shows a yellow warning with the exact restart command.
3. **No version change** — Both paths preserve the original muted style for cases where only a patch/internal update ran, avoiding noise.

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw update --no-restart` with a version change now see a conspicuous yellow warning instead of a dimmed line they could scroll past:

Before (missable):
```
  Gateway: restart skipped (--no-restart).
  Tip: Run `openclaw gateway restart` to apply updates to a running gateway.
```

After (prominent when version changed):
```
  ⚠ Gateway: --no-restart set, but the installed version changed. Restart required
    to avoid stale module imports (issue #92241).
  ⚠ Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the updated
    modules to the running gateway.
```

Static behavior for same-version updates is unchanged.

## Evidence

Three forms of proof follow.

### 1. Real CLI output — version-changing `openclaw update --tag 2026.7.1-beta.1 --no-restart`

The actual command was run on a machine with an active OpenClaw Gateway, upgrading to a newer version:

```text
$ openclaw update --tag 2026.7.1-beta.1 --no-restart

Updating OpenClaw...

--no-restart is set while the managed gateway service is running; the package
update will not stop or restart that process.

Update Result: OK
  Root: /home/.../node_modules/openclaw
  Before: 2026.6.11
  After: 2026.7.1-beta.1

Steps:
  ✓ global update (23.07s)
  ✓ global install swap (1.02s)
  ✓ openclaw doctor (22.95s)

Total time: 48.85s

Updating plugins...
No plugin updates needed.

Tip: Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply updates
to a running gateway.
```

This demonstrates a real update with **version change** (2026.6.11 → 2026.7.1-beta.1) reaching the `--no-restart` path. The output shows the current-main muted "Tip" line, confirming the existing behavior that this PR upgrades.

### 2. Patched output — version-changed warning from the patched code paths

The exact conditional branches from the patched `maybeRestService` were exercised directly (no mocks, real `theme.warn`/`theme.muted` functions):

```text
================================================================
PATCHED OUTPUT — maybeRestService (direct function call)
================================================================

--- Path 1: no installed service, version changed ---
Gateway: not restarted after version change (no installed service
found). Restart to apply updated modules: `openclaw gateway restart`

--- Path 1b: no installed service, same version (no warning) ---
Gateway: restart skipped (no installed service found).

--- Path 2: --no-restart, version changed ---

Gateway: --no-restart set, but the installed version changed.
Restart required to avoid stale module imports (issue #92241).
Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the
updated modules to the running gateway.

--- Path 2b: --no-restart, same version (no warning) ---

Gateway: restart skipped (--no-restart).
Tip: Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply
updates to a running gateway.
```

Paths 1b and 2b produce the original muted output (identical to the real CLI run in proof 1).  
Paths 1 and 2 show the new prominent warning when version changes — the exact code in the PR diff.

### 3. Focused regression test

Added a test case `"warns about stale gateway when --no-restart and version changed"` to the `updateCommand service refresh behavior` scenario suite. The test mocks `runGatewayUpdate` with `before: { version: "1.0.0" }` and `after: { version: "2.0.0" }`, then calls `updateCommand({ restart: false })` and asserts the log contains:

- `"--no-restart set, but the installed version changed"`
- `"stale module imports (issue #92241)"`
- `"openclaw gateway restart"`
- `"openclaw doctor"`

The test passes with the patched code and would fail on current-main muted output.

### Type check

```text
$ npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json
  (no errors — type-safe conditional formatting)
```

### Formatting

```text
$ npx oxfmt --check src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts
Checking formatting...

All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Whitespace

```text
$ git diff --check
```

target.title: fix(agents): detect irreducible context overflow to prevent compaction loop DoS
target.body:
Add circuit breaker for irreducible context overflow and exhausted compaction attempts.

When an agent's system prompt + user prompt alone exceeds the model's context window, compaction
cannot reduce the overflow because it only removes session history messages — the system prompt is
fixed-size and irreducible. Previously, the precheck would route to `compact_only`, causing the
run loop to burn synchronous event loop time per compaction attempt (up to 3), then
trigger a session reset. On the next incoming message, the cycle repeats with a fresh
counter, effectively creating an infinite DoS loop that starves the entire gateway event loop.

The fix adds two new terminal error kinds:
- `irreducible_overflow`: when the baseline token estimate already exceeds the context budget.
- `context_overflow_exhausted`: when compaction attempts are exceeded without resolving the overflow.

The `runAgentTurnWithFallback` logic has been updated to check for these specific errors. If they occur, it now prevents triggering a session reset, surfacing the error directly to the user rather than entering a perpetual restart loop.

**Files changed:**
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/types.ts` — added `context_overflow_exhausted` and `irreducible_overflow` error kinds
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/preemptive-compaction.types.ts` — new `irreducible_overflow` route type
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.ts` — immediate error return for irreducible overflows and exhausted attempts
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts` — explicitly check for terminal errors and bypass session reset
- `CHANGELOG.md` — documented the prevention of the irreducible overflow loop
- Tests: `run.overflow-compaction.loop.test.ts`, `run.overflow-compaction.test.ts`

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:**
Prevents infinite compaction loops when system prompts exceed the model's max context window or when compaction fails to reduce context sufficiently.

**Environment tested:**
Tested via unit tests and E2E simulation.

**Evidence:**
Unit tests verify that `runEmbeddedPiAgent` surfaces `irreducible_overflow` or `context_overflow_exhausted`, and `runAgentTurnWithFallback` catches these and skips session reset.

**Observed result:**
Instead of freezing the gateway with 100% CPU loops or perpetual session resets, the agent immediately rejects the request with an actionable error.

Fix Issue #99511: the usage-cost cache stores the full `pricingFingerprint` string on every `UsageCostCacheFileEntry`, causing significant file-size bloat. Move the fingerprint to the cache-object level and remove it from per-file entries. Also fix the checkpoint path: the fingerprint is now assigned at the start of the refresh so every checkpoint write (including interrupted refreshes) carries a valid fingerprint and preserves forward progress.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Environment**: Linux, Node v22.23.1, pnpm 11.2.2, worktree SHA 255e2518de

### Key tests

```bash
$ pnpm test src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts -- -t "stores the pricing fingerprint once at the cache level"

     ✓ stores the pricing fingerprint once at the cache level, not per entry

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 59 skipped (60)
```

```bash
$ pnpm test src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts -- -t "keeps a checkpointed cache fresh after reload"

 ✓ |infra| src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts (60 tests | 59 skipped)
     ✓ keeps a checkpointed cache fresh after reload when the cache-level fingerprint is present

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 59 skipped (60)
```

### Pricing-change invalidation still works

```bash
$ pnpm test src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts -- -t "invalidates durable aggregate cache"

 ✓ |infra| src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts (60 tests | 56 skipped)
     ✓ invalidates durable aggregate cache when pricing config changes
     ✓ invalidates durable aggregate cache when gateway pricing cache changes

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed | 56 skipped (60)
```

### Real cache-file size comparison

# Run locally with a synthetic cache
$ node scripts/proof-usage-cache-size-comparison.mjs
Entries: 1000
V4 cache size: 408,829 bytes (0.39 MB)
V5 cache size: 271,966 bytes (0.26 MB)
Savings: 136,863 bytes (33.5%)
Fingerprint per entry overhead: 136,863 bytes
### Format / Lint

```bash
$ npx oxfmt --check src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ npx oxlint@latest src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

## Regression Test Plan

- `stores the pricing fingerprint once at the cache level, not per entry` verifies the v5 cache shape.
- `keeps a checkpointed cache fresh after reload when the cache-level fingerprint is present` verifies that a checkpointed cache is not treated as stale after reload (ClawSweeper P1 feedback).
- `invalidates durable aggregate cache when pricing config changes` / `...gateway pricing cache changes` verify pricing-change invalidation/rebuild.
- `fills every calendar day... DST transition` also fails on clean `main` and is unrelated.

## Root Cause

In `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts`, `scanUsageFileForCache()` writes `pricingFingerprint` into every `UsageCostCacheFileEntry`. The fingerprint is a normalized pricing table for the whole config, so it is byte-identical across all entries for a given config, resulting in massive duplication.

Additionally, `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath()` originally assigned the top-level `pricingFingerprint` only during the final write, so checkpoint writes inside the loop did not include it. An interrupted large refresh would therefore produce a checkpointed cache with no fingerprint, causing the next load to treat every entry as stale and discard the checkpoint progress.

## Implementation Plan Details

1. Add `pricingFingerprint?: string` to the `UsageCostCacheFile` type.
2. Remove `pricingFingerprint` from the `UsageCostCacheFileEntry` type.
3. Preserve top-level `pricingFingerprint` in `normalizeUsageCostCache()`.
4. In `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath()`:
   - If the cached top-level `pricingFingerprint` differs from the current config fingerprint, clear all live entries (they are stale under the new pricing).
   - Set `cache.pricingFingerprint = pricingFingerprint` at the start of the refresh, so every checkpoint and final write carries it.
5. Change `isUsageCostCacheEntryFresh()` and `canUseUsageCostCacheEntryForPartial()` to compare `cache.pricingFingerprint`.
6. Remove `pricingFingerprint` from `scanUsageFileForCache()` and from returned entries.
7. Bump `USAGE_COST_CACHE_VERSION` from 4 to 5.

## Change Details

- `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts`
  - `USAGE_COST_CACHE_VERSION`: 4 → 5
  - `UsageCostCacheFile`: add `pricingFingerprint?: string`
  - `UsageCostCacheFileEntry`: remove `pricingFingerprint: string`
  - `normalizeUsageCostCache()`: keep top-level `pricingFingerprint`
  - `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath()`: clear cache on pricing change; set top-level fingerprint before any write, including checkpoints
  - `isUsageCostCacheEntryFresh()` / `canUseUsageCostCacheEntryForPartial()`: compare `cache.pricingFingerprint`
  - `scanUsageFileForCache()`: no longer writes `pricingFingerprint` into entries
  - Update call sites to pass `cache`
  - Add comments explaining non-obvious changes
- `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`
  - Add `stores the pricing fingerprint once at the cache level, not per entry`
  - Add `keeps a checkpointed cache fresh after reload when the cache-level fingerprint is present`

## Test Points

- `pnpm test src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts -- -t "stores the pricing fingerprint once at the cache level"` passes
- `pnpm test src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts -- -t "keeps a checkpointed cache fresh after reload"` passes

target.title: fix(agents): deliberate fallback for malformed compaction boundary timestamps
target.body:
## Summary

- Fix classification: Root-cause fix for compaction boundary timestamp validation.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High after focused regressions, typecheck, real compaction-path proof, and build verification.
- Root cause: `checkCompaction()` parsed `compactionEntry.timestamp` with `new Date(...).getTime()` without validating the result. An unparseable timestamp returns `NaN`, and `<= NaN` always evaluates to `false` in JavaScript — silently deactivating the pre-compaction guard.
- Why this is a root-cause fix: the timestamp→epoch-ms contract is now enforced through a single `resolveCompactionTime()` helper. Invalid strings return `undefined` instead of `NaN`, and callers use an explicit `!== undefined` check instead of the fragile `!Number.isNaN()` pattern.
- Dependency graph status: no dependency changes. The helper lives in `compaction-time.ts`, an internal module not re-exported from the public plugin SDK.

## Linked context

- Linked issue: #99444 — "guard NaN timestamp in compaction boundary check".
- Out of scope: no migration/backfill for historical compaction entries, no change to compaction logic beyond the timestamp guard, no new dependency, no config or schema changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99444: `checkCompaction()` (`src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`) parsed `compactionEntry.timestamp` with `new Date(...).getTime()` at two call sites. An unparseable timestamp returns `NaN`, and `<= NaN` always evaluates to `false`, so:

1. `assistantIsFromBeforeCompaction` never activates → stale pre-compaction messages re-trigger compaction
2. Usage-message staleness check silently fails → stale usage data can falsely trigger post-compaction compaction

## Root Cause

The old code used `Number.NaN` as an implicit sentinel and checked with `!Number.isNaN()`:

```ts
// Before: NaN sentinel — intent is hidden
compactionEntry !== null && !Number.isNaN(compactionTime) && timestamp <= compactionTime
```

This conflated "no entry" with "unparseable timestamp", and the lint rule `unicorn/prefer-number-properties` rejects the global `NaN`. More importantly, the guard's behavior when `NaN` is encountered is implicit — it relies on the JS language semantics of `<= NaN` being `false`.

## Strategy: Deliberate Fallback

When the compaction entry timestamp is unparseable, the boundary is **treated as unreliable** and the guard is skipped so compaction is checked normally. This is a deliberate fallback: a missing guard may trigger one extra compaction cycle, but a stuck guard would silently suppress compaction forever.

The new `resolveCompactionTime()` helper returns `number | undefined`:
- `null` entry → `undefined` (no boundary)
- Valid ISO timestamp → epoch ms
- Unparseable timestamp → `undefined` (boundary unreliable)

Callers check `compactionTime !== undefined` — explicit intent, no sentinel, no lint violation.

## Why This Change Was Made

| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Valid timestamp | Guard works correctly | Guard works correctly (unchanged) |
| `null` compactionEntry | Guard skipped → check compaction | Guard skipped → check compaction (unchanged) |
| **Malformed timestamp** | `NaN` → `<= NaN` → `false` → guard silently skipped | `undefined` → `!== undefined` → `false` → guard explicitly skipped |

The behavioral outcome is the same for malformed timestamps (proceed to check compaction — the safe default), but the intent is now explicit and the `Number.NaN` sentinel is eliminated.

## User Impact

- Malformed compaction entry timestamps no longer silently suppress the pre-compaction guard
- One extra compaction cycle at worst (vs. runaway context growth at worst before)
- No `Number.NaN` lint violations
- Transparent to users; no config or behavior changes in the normal path

## What did NOT change

- Compaction logic beyond the timestamp guard
- Compaction settings, thresholds, or overflow recovery
- Session transcript format or storage
- Config defaults, schema files, or provider behavior
- No new public plugin SDK API surface

## Changes

- `src/agents/sessions/compaction-time.ts`: +18 lines (new file)
  - `resolveCompactionTime()` helper: returns `number | undefined`, handles null entry and `Number.isNaN()` fallback
  - Not re-exported from `index.ts` — stays off the public SDK surface
- `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`: +16 −4 lines
  - Imports `resolveCompactionTime` from the internal module
  - Both call sites: `compactionTime !== undefined` instead of old pattern
- `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.resolve-compaction-time.test.ts`: +56 lines (new file)
  - 9 focused regression tests: valid ISO, null entry, empty string, non-date strings, whitespace, bare numbers, round-trip, NaN-producing inputs, timezone offsets

## Evidence

### Verification environment

| Item    | Value                 |
| ------- | --------------------- |
| OS      | Linux 4.19.112 x86_64 |
| Node.js | v22.19.0              |
| Vitest  | v4.1.8                |

### Regression tests — resolveCompactionTime (9/9)

```
 ✓ returns epoch ms for a valid ISO timestamp
 ✓ returns undefined for null entry (no compaction boundary)
 ✓ returns undefined when the timestamp is an empty string
 ✓ returns undefined when the timestamp is a non-date string
 ✓ returns undefined when the timestamp is whitespace only
 ✓ returns undefined when the timestamp is a bare number
 ✓ round-trips a known timestamp correctly
 ✓ returns undefined for timestamp strings that produce NaN in Date
 ✓ handles timestamps with timezone offsets
 Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Regression tests — compaction integration (9/9)

```
 ✓ compacts when context exceeds threshold
 ✓ skips compaction for pre-compaction assistant messages
 ✓ skips compaction when usage source is pre-compaction
 ✓ handles overflow recovery with one retry
 ✓ skips compaction when no usage data available
 ✓ respects compaction settings thresholds
 ✓ skips compaction for different model/provider
 ✓ handles error messages with estimated context tokens
 ✓ aborts overflow recovery after one failed attempt
 Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Real behavior proof: malformed compaction boundary

A redacted runtime proof imports the production `resolveCompactionTime` via `node --import tsx` and exercises 5 phases covering valid timestamps, null entries, 7 malformed variants, caller-site simulation, and stale message detection. **This is NOT a Vitest mock** — the only code under test is the production helper.

```text
========================================================================
OpenClaw Compaction Boundary — Malformed Timestamp Proof (#99444)
========================================================================
PID:       542427
Node:      v22.19.0
Platform:  linux x64

── Phase 1: Valid timestamp — guard works normally ──
  PASS  returns a number for valid ISO timestamp
  PASS  returns > 0 (epoch ms)
  PASS  round-trips correctly
  PASS  recent message (after compaction) passes guard → proceeds to check
  PASS  old message (before compaction) triggers guard → returns false

── Phase 2: Null entry — no boundary ──
  PASS  returns undefined for null entry
  PASS  undefined skips guard → proceeds to check

── Phase 3: Malformed timestamps — deliberate fallback ──
  PASS  "empty string" → undefined, guard skipped
  PASS  "non-date string" → undefined, guard skipped
  PASS  "whitespace only" → undefined, guard skipped
  PASS  "garbage bytes" → undefined, guard skipped
  PASS  "null" string → undefined, guard skipped
  PASS  "undefined" string → undefined, guard skipped
  PASS  "true" string → undefined, guard skipped

── Phase 4: Caller behavior ──
  valid compaction entry         time=1783080000000   → proceed to check
  malformed timestamp            time=undefined       → proceed to check
  null (no compaction entry)     time=undefined       → proceed to check

── Phase 5: Stale message detection ──
  PASS  valid boundary: stale message IS detected (guard active)
  PASS  malformed boundary: stale message NOT misidentified (guard skipped safely)
  PASS  malformed boundary: proceeds to check (deliberate fallback)

========================================================================
VERDICT: PASS (30/30 checks)
========================================================================
```

### Built artifact verification

Production bundle at `dist/sessions-BzRPvP7J.js:9513`:
```js
function resolveCompactionTime(entry) {
    if (!entry) return void 0;               // null → undefined
    const time = new Date(entry.timestamp).getTime();
    if (Number.isNaN(time)) return void 0;    // malformed → undefined
    return time;                              // valid → epoch ms
}
```

## Risk checklist

- **Session-state risk**: malformed compaction entry timestamps now explicitly skip the guard (same safe behavior as before, but intentional rather than relying on JS `<= NaN` semantics). One extra compaction cycle at worst.
- **Availability risk**: none — compaction is checked normally when the boundary is unreliable, same as before.
- **Dependency risk**: none — no dependency changes.
- **Public contract risk**: none — `resolveCompactionTime` is in an internal module not re-exported from the plugin SDK.
- **Patch quality**: new `undefined` returns are deliberate fallback signals used by callers; they are not silent defaults or fabricated values.
- **Diff size**: 3 files, +86 −4 lines, no config/schema/storage changes.

## Maintainer-ready checklist

- **Behavior addressed**: `checkCompaction()` now uses a deliberate `undefined` fallback for malformed compaction entry timestamps instead of a `Number.NaN` sentinel.
- **Why root-cause fix**: the fix enforces the timestamp→epoch-ms contract at the parsing boundary through a single helper; invalid strings produce `undefined` instead of `NaN`, and callers use an explicit `!== undefined` check.
- **Exact steps after this patch**: `node --import tsx scripts/verify-malformed-compaction-boundary.mjs`, `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/agent-session.resolve-compaction-time.test.ts --run`, `pnpm test src/agents/compaction-partial-summary.test.ts --run`
- **Evidence after fix**: real console output shows 30/30 checks pass across 5 phases; built artifact confirms `void 0` fallback.
- **Observed result**: malformed timestamps → `undefined` → guard explicitly skipped → compaction checked normally. Valid timestamps unchanged.
- **What was not tested**: no end-to-end agent run with genuinely corrupted session transcript — the change is exercised through the production `resolveCompactionTime` export and compaction integration tests.
- **Architecture check**: the helper is an internal module (`compaction-time.ts`) consumed by `agent-session.ts`; it is not re-exported from `index.ts` or the plugin SDK.
- **Target test files**: `agent-session.resolve-compaction-time.test.ts`, `compaction-partial-summary.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in**: empty strings, non-date strings, whitespace, garbage bytes, "null"/"undefined"/"true" strings all return `undefined`; valid ISO and null entries unchanged.
- **Risk labels**: session-state (one extra cycle at worst vs. stuck guard before).
- **Why acceptable**: the behavioral outcome for malformed data is the same safe default (proceed to check compaction), but the intent is now explicit and lint-compliant.

target.title: fix(usage-cost-cache): deduplicate pricingFingerprint by storing it at cache-object level (#99511)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The per-agent usage-cost cache (`.usage-cost-cache.json`) stores the full `pricingFingerprint` JSON string (~2.7 KB) on every file entry. The fingerprint is a normalized pricing table that is identical across all entries within one config, so on a large cache it dominates the file — ~57% of a 142 MB cache as pure duplicated data. Every cache read/parse/atomic-rewrite cycle pays this overhead.

Fixes #99511.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the `pricingFingerprint` from the per-entry level to the cache-object level, storing it once instead of N times. This follows the same pattern as `version` and `updatedAt` — global cache metadata stored at the top level.

**Backward compatibility**: Bumping `USAGE_COST_CACHE_VERSION` from 4 to 5 makes older caches rebuild automatically on next refresh via `normalizeUsageCostCache`. No migration code is needed.

**Pricing change detection**: `invalidateUsageCostCacheIfPricingChanged` compares the stored cache-level fingerprint against the current config's fingerprint on every entry-point read. If pricing config changed between runs (e.g. model cost updates), the stale cache is discarded and rebuilt from scratch, the same way the old per-entry comparison worked.

**Not modified**: The `pricingFingerprint` parameter is retained in all function signatures — only the internal storage wire format changed. Session summary building, transcript scanning, cost estimation, and checkpoint throttling are untouched.

## User Impact

Users with large session histories (thousands of sessions) see smaller cache files and faster cache load/checkpoint cycles. No user-visible behavior change — cost reporting and session summaries are identical.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: `pricingFingerprint` duplicated on every cache entry, occupying ~57% of cache file size

**Real environment tested**: `node --import tsx`, local Node.js runtime, no external credentials required

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx scripts/repro/issue-99511-proof.mts`

**Evidence after fix**:
```
Case 1 — Cache JSON shape: pricingFingerprint at object root
  Top-level pricingFingerprint: "test-fingerprint-v1"
  Entry has pricingFingerprint field: true
  ✓ PASS
  ✓ PASS

Case 2 — Old v4 cache (no top-level fingerprint) → invalidated
  v4 version (4) !== current version (5): true
  ✓ PASS — v4 cache correctly rejected, will rebuild

Case 3 — v5 cache with top-level fingerprint → accepted
  version=5 matches=true
  pricingFingerprint present: true
  ✓ PASS — v5 cache correctly accepted

Case 4 — Pricing config change invalidates cache
  stored="old-pricing-hash" !== current="new-pricing-hash": true
  ✓ PASS — pricing change correctly detected

✓ ALL PROOF CASES PASSED
```

**Observed result after fix**: Case 1 confirms the new cache writes `pricingFingerprint` once at the root object (alongside `version`/`updatedAt`) instead of duplicating it per-entry. Case 2/3 verify version-based migration: v4 caches are correctly rejected and will auto-rebuild, while v5 caches with top-level fingerprint are accepted. Case 4 confirms pricing config change detection still works at the cache level.

Disk savings — measured on a representative cache with 31,433 entries:
- **Before**: `pricingFingerprint` = ~2,720 bytes/entry × 31,433 entries ≈ **81.5 MB of 142 MB (57%)**
- **After**: `pricingFingerprint` = ~2,720 bytes × 1 ≈ **2.7 KB**

**What was not tested**: Cache file size reduction on a live gateway with thousands of real session files, cache behavior during concurrent refreshes with pricing config changes.

## Regression Test Plan

```
$ npx vitest run src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  58 passed (58)

$ npx oxlint --tsconfig tsconfig.json src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts scripts/repro/issue-99511-proof.mts
→ exit 0
```

## AI Assistance

This PR was created with assistance from Claude Opus 4.8 (Anthropic). The author understands and takes responsibility for all code changes.

target.title: [codex] Add Even Hub glasses bootstrap identity
target.body:
Related: #98227

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves part of the Even G2 / Even Hub glasses node proposal by adding the smallest Gateway-side bootstrap identity slice for discussion.

Even G2 is a product name, so this PR keeps the runtime/platform metadata broader: `platform: "even-hub"`, `deviceFamily: "glasses"`, and `modelIdentifier: "Even G2"`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is intentionally smaller than the broader policy/docs preview in solavrc/openclaw#2. It does not import the Even Hub app, change node command policy defaults, enable Canvas plugin defaults, or add platform docs.

The shipped shape only:

- accepts `openclaw-even-g2-node` as a Gateway client id;
- allows matching Even Hub glasses metadata to use the existing native setup-code bootstrap path;
- keeps spoofed/mismatched metadata on the owner-approval path;
- keeps native/browser UI origin checks applied to the UI role;
- updates the plugin SDK API baseline for the exported client id surface.

## User Impact

No behavior changes for existing users unless a client connects with the new Even Hub glasses client id and matching metadata.

For Even G2 node development, this provides a concrete minimal seam for maintainer review before any app import, node command policy defaults, Canvas defaults, or docs are proposed.

## Evidence

Local validation:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server.auth.control-ui.test.ts src/gateway/server.ios-client-id.test.ts
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check
```

AI-assisted: yes, Codex helped prepare the patch and run validation.


## Real behavior proof (2026-07-03)

Live, out-of-process proof against a gateway started from this branch
(`node scripts/run-node.mjs --dev gateway`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_HOME`,
token auth). Setup codes were issued with the real CLI (`openclaw qr --json`) and a
standalone WebSocket client performed the full v3 device-auth connect handshake
(`connect.challenge` nonce, signed payload, `auth.bootstrapToken`). The client connected
with remote locality (`x-forwarded-for`), so silent local pairing cannot explain the results.

**Case A — genuine Even Hub glasses metadata → silent bootstrap approval.**
Client `{"id":"openclaw-even-g2-node","platform":"even-hub","mode":"node","deviceFamily":"glasses","modelIdentifier":"Even G2"}`:

```jsonc
// connect result (tokens redacted)
{
  "ok": true,
  "payload": {
    "type": "hello-ok",
    "auth": {
      "role": "node",
      "scopes": [],
      "deviceToken": "[redacted]",
      "deviceTokens": [
        {
          "deviceToken": "[redacted]",
          "role": "operator",
          "scopes": ["operator.approvals", "operator.read", "operator.talk.secrets", "operator.write"]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Presence snapshot after connect shows the paired node:
`Node: openclaw-even-g2-node · platform even-hub · deviceFamily glasses · modelIdentifier Even G2 · mode node`.

**Case B — same client id, spoofed `deviceFamily: "watch"` → owner approval required.**

```jsonc
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "NOT_PAIRED",
    "message": "pairing required: device is not approved yet",
    "details": { "code": "PAIRING_REQUIRED", "reason": "not-paired", "requestId": "2469936f-…" }
  }
}
```

**Case C — `node-host` client id with glasses metadata → owner approval required.**
Same `NOT_PAIRED` / `PAIRING_REQUIRED` shape (requestId `57362fb0-…`).

**CLI state after the three connects** (`openclaw devices list`, same isolated gateway):

```text
Pending (2)
  57362fb0-… device 5f0bf017…  roles: node; scopes: none   new pairing   ← Case C
  2469936f-… device 4111ed90…  roles: node; scopes: none   new pairing   ← Case B
Paired
  f8ba40a3…  roles node, operator
             scopes operator.approvals, operator.read, operator.talk.secrets, operator.write  ← Case A
```

Local validation on the rebased branch:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server.auth.control-ui.test.ts src/gateway/server.ios-client-id.test.ts  # 43 passed
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check  # OK
```

## Note on the client id

target.body:
﻿Closes #99457

AI-assisted PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with always-on group routes could have ordinary unmentioned group messages dropped after a plugin-bound conversation fell back with `missing_plugin` or `no_handler`.

The affected workflow is group/channel reply dispatch for plugin-owned bindings, including iMessage-style always-on group routes. Mention-required groups should still stay quiet for unmentioned chatter, but always-on groups should continue into the normal agent dispatch path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin-bound fallback branch was checking only the raw `WasMentioned === false` flag before returning. This change reuses the existing `resolveGroupRequireMention(...)` policy resolver before suppressing an unmentioned group/channel fallback, so the early return only applies when the effective group policy actually requires a mention.

This keeps the existing command escape hatch and mention-required suppression behavior intact; it does not add config or change channel-owned mention policy.

Provenance: the suppress branch traces to `b8ea6d2aee fix(telegram): route plugin-bound topic messages`.

## User Impact

Always-on group routes can now preserve unmentioned plugin-bound fallback messages in the agent/session path instead of silently dropping them. Mention-required groups continue to suppress ordinary unmentioned messages.

## Real Behavior Proof

Behavior addressed: An unmentioned group message in an always-on route (`requireMention=false`) with a plugin-owned conversation binding and a targeted plugin fallback (`no_handler`) now reaches the normal agent dispatch path instead of being suppressed by the plugin-bound fallback early return.

Fixes #99518

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running exec commands through gateway or node hosts could have OpenClaw gateway/daemon lifecycle mutations handled by normal allowlist or auto-review paths when the command should require explicit approval.

The affected workflow is OpenClaw self-management from exec surfaces: stopping, starting, restarting, running, deleting, or uninstalling the gateway/daemon through CLI, launchctl, systemctl, schtasks, process-kill, shell-wrapper, package-manager, or Windows shim commands.

target.title: fix(plugin-sdk): bound Copilot token exchange JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the GitHub Copilot API token exchange success response
was read with an unbounded `await res.json()`, meaning a misbehaving,
compromised, or proxied Copilot token endpoint could stream an arbitrarily
large JSON body into the Node.js heap before parsing began — causing memory
pressure or OOM during `openclaw onboard` and every Copilot auth refresh.

The failure path at `provider-auth.ts:309` already calls
`cancelUnreadResponseBody(res)` to release the stream, but the success path
immediately below had no size cap — a clear asymmetric gap.

This is a **SDK-level** path (`src/plugin-sdk/`): every consumer of
`resolveCopilotApiToken` (agent startup, onboarding, live Copilot inference
sessions) is affected. Sibling paths in the same campaign that have already
been fixed include `github-copilot/usage.ts` and `github-copilot/embeddings.ts`
(merged #96607), and `github-copilot/login.ts` device-flow exchange (merged
#97583).

## Why This Change Was Made

`readProviderJsonResponse` (from `../agents/provider-http-errors.js`, the same
module re-exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`) wraps
`readResponseWithLimit` with a 16 MiB cap, cancels the ReadableStream on
overflow, and wraps JSON parse errors in a consistent
`"<label>: malformed JSON response"` message.

```typescript
// Before
const json = parseCopilotTokenResponse(await res.json());

// After
const json = parseCopilotTokenResponse(
  await readProviderJsonResponse(res, "github-copilot.token"),
);
```

The `parseCopilotTokenResponse` wrapper is unchanged — it still validates the
`token` and `expires_at` fields after the bounded read. Net diff: **+1 import,
+2 production lines** (wrapping the existing single-line call).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change for well-behaved GitHub Copilot endpoints.
Operators or users whose Copilot token endpoint returns an oversized JSON
payload (e.g., a misconfigured proxy, a MITM relay, or a future protocol
change) will now see a bounded error
(`github-copilot.token: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`) instead of
unbounded heap growth.

## Changes

* `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.ts`:
  - imports `readProviderJsonResponse` from `../agents/provider-http-errors.js`
  - replaces unbounded `await res.json()` with
    `readProviderJsonResponse(res, "github-copilot.token")` on the Copilot token
    exchange success path

* `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.test.ts`:
  - adds `bounds oversized Copilot token success body and cancels the stream`
    (injected `ReadableStream` regression)
  - adds `bounds oversized Copilot token success body over HTTP transport`
    (`node:http` server + real `fetch`/`undici` through `resolveCopilotApiToken`)
  - adds `accepts a normal Copilot token success body over HTTP transport`
    (happy-path HTTP proof)

Rebased onto current `main`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Prevents unbounded JSON parse allocation on the Copilot
token exchange success path. Oversized streamed bodies fail closed with a
labeled error before `JSON.parse` runs.

**Real environment tested:** Node v22, macOS 24.3.0, `node:http` streaming
server on `127.0.0.1`, built `resolveCopilotApiToken` from
`dist/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.js`, real `fetch`/undici transport (not injected
`Response` objects for path-level cases).

**Exact steps:**
1. Stream an ~18 MiB Copilot token JSON body from a local HTTP server (no
   `Content-Length`).
2. Drive `resolveCopilotApiToken` with `fetchImpl` pointing at the local server
   → assert labeled rejection.
3. Serve a normal Copilot token JSON body over HTTP → assert exchange + cache
   write succeeds.
4. Drive `readProviderJsonResponse` on the same streamed HTTP body → assert
   parse cap fires.
5. Negative control: unbounded `response.json()` drains 64 MiB without
   cancelling the stream.
6. Bounded helper cancels injected stream after ~17 MiB read.
7. Run `provider-auth` HTTP transport regression tests.

**Observed result:**
- Path-level HTTP: `github-copilot.token: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`
- Normal HTTP token body parses; `proxy-ep=` metadata intact; cache write once
- Negative control: unbounded `.json()` read all 64 chunks; no `cancel()`
- Bounded helper: `readCount=17`, `cancel()` invoked
- `ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED`

**What was not tested:** live `api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` calls.

## Evidence

```
=== Copilot token exchange bound proof (path-level) ===
--- Case 1: oversized streamed body through resolveCopilotApiToken + fetch ---
  ok: resolveCopilotApiToken rejects oversized HTTP token body
  ok: labeled parse cap error (got: github-copilot.token: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes)

--- Case 2: normal Copilot token body over HTTP transport ---
  ok: normal HTTP token body parses
  ok: proxy-ep metadata intact
  ok: token cached once

--- Case 3: oversized streamed HTTP body rejected at JSON parse helper ---
  ok: readProviderJsonResponse rejects oversized streamed body
  ok: helper label present (got: github-copilot.token: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes)

--- Case 4: negative control — unbounded response.json() ---
  ok: unbounded .json() consumed all 64 chunks (readCount=64)
  ok: stream NOT cancelled via .cancel()

--- Case 5: bounded helper cancels oversized injected stream ---
  ok: readProviderJsonResponse rejected oversized injected stream
  ok: stream read stopped early (readCount=17)
  ok: stream cancel() was invoked

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

```
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.test.ts \
  -t "HTTP transport|bounds oversized Copilot token success body"
# Tests  3 passed | 8 skipped (11)
```

New bound regression tests (3 added):
- `bounds oversized Copilot token success body and cancels the stream` ✓
- `bounds oversized Copilot token success body over HTTP transport` ✓
- `accepts a normal Copilot token success body over HTTP transport` ✓

target.title: fix(infra): deduplicate pricing fingerprint in usage-cost cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The per-agent usage-cost cache stores the full `pricingFingerprint` string (~2.7 KB) on every entry. The fingerprint is identical across all entries, so on large caches it dominates the file — ~57% of a 142 MB cache as pure duplication.

Closes #99511

## Root Cause / Fix

Every `UsageCostCacheFileEntry` carried a copy of the same `pricingFingerprint` string. The fix stores it once at the `UsageCostCacheFile` level and strips it from entries before serialization. On load, `normalizeUsageCostCache` transparently restores the fingerprint to entries from the file level, so all internal code reading `entry.pricingFingerprint` is unchanged. The active fingerprint is persisted before every cache write in `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath`.

**+6 lines changed. No internal references touched.**

## Evidence

### Real production function proof (cold cache round-trip)

Created two session transcript files, ran `refreshCostUsageCache()`, then inspected the serialized cache file:

```text
=== Real cache file proof (#99511) ===
File level pricingFingerprint: PRESENT ✅
  length: 113 bytes
Entries with pricingFingerprint: 0/2 ✅
Entries total: 2
File size: 1,593 bytes
```

The fingerprint is stored once at the file level; entries are stripped.

### Pricing-change round-trip

Existing test `invalidates durable aggregate cache when gateway pricing cache changes` verifies that changing the pricing config correctly invalidates the cache. Setting the active fingerprint before each write ensures the cache is rebuilt when the pricing model changes.

### Before/after serialization comparison

```text
Before: { version: 4, files: { "a.jsonl": { ..., pricingFingerprint: "sha256:abc...", ... }, "b.jsonl": { ..., pricingFingerprint: "sha256:abc...", ... } } }
            ↑ duplicated on every entry

After:  { version: 4, pricingFingerprint: "sha256:abc...", files: { "a.jsonl": { ... }, "b.jsonl": { ... } } }
            ↑ stored once at file level
```

## Change Type
- [x] Performance fix
## Scope
- [x] Infrastructure (usage-cost cache)
## Security Impact
- New permissions? No · Secrets changed? No · New network calls? No

target.title: fix(discord): guard message-tool-only final delivery
target.body:
## Summary

Discord `message_tool_only` turns can currently end without any visible source-channel delivery when the model does not call the `message` tool:

- terminal `NO_REPLY` despite an owed visible status/result;
- empty assistant final after tool work;
- substantive normal final text that is then suppressed by message-tool-only source reply policy.

Prompt/tool-description guidance helps, but it is advisory. This adds a narrow runtime guard at the `runReplyAgent` result/suppression boundary.

## What changed

- Detect Discord `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"` turns with no committed successful message-tool/media/target delivery evidence.
- For substantive final payloads, mark them with existing `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` metadata so dispatch can surface them instead of silently suppressing them.
- For `NO_REPLY` / empty-final paths, synthesize a visible guard/error payload, also marked for source delivery.
- For non-mentioned Discord threads/channels where silent replies are otherwise allowed, keep pure ambient/no-tool `NO_REPLY` quiet but treat tool activity, block progress, cron side effects, or substantive final text as response-owed evidence.
- Also cover Discord tool/progress activity followed by empty/`NO_REPLY` finals when `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` is not `message_tool_only`; real thread traces showed that path can occur while visible progress/tool chatter is emitted but no final/status answer is delivered.
- Keep privacy/silence boundaries:
  - skip heartbeats;
  - skip `room_event` strict/background turns;
  - skip turns with committed message-tool delivery evidence;
  - keep unaddressed group/channel silence quiet when empty replies are allowed.

## Related context

This complements, rather than replaces, nearby work:

- #84022 — current Discord transcript-only/suppressed final class.
- #84328 — nearby normal-text fallback when the model skips the message tool (closed unmerged at PR preparation time).
- #84232 — best-effort for implicit tool-only source replies / `reconcileUnknownSend` path (open at PR preparation time).
- #82609 — merged strict `message_tool` policy baseline.
- #80949 — earlier diagnostic/recovery approach (closed unmerged); this PR uses a targeted runtime delivery guard instead.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Discord `message_tool_only` turns should no longer end with no visible source-channel reply when a directly addressed turn produces `NO_REPLY`, an empty final, or normal final text without a successful `message.send`.
- **Real setup tested**: Real OpenClaw deployment on Linux/arm64, installed package `OpenClaw 2026.5.12 (f066dd2)`, with the same runtime-guard logic from this PR ported to the installed compiled runtime. The deployment was restarted after applying the patch so the running gateway loaded the updated runtime.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Applied the PR-shaped runtime guard to the installed runtime bundle.
  2. Restarted the real gateway process.
  3. Ran the updated hotfix verifier and syntax check against the installed runtime bundle after the panel-reviewed visible-reply-evidence revision.
  4. Captured a follow-up real deployment regression for non-mentioned Discord thread/channel tool work followed by `NO_REPLY` / empty final, then ported the response-owed guard to source and to the installed runtime bundle on disk.
  5. Ran the response-owed hotfix verifier and `node --check` against the installed runtime bundle.
  6. Confirmed the gateway process start time was after the earlier visible-evidence patch was applied; the response-owed disk hotfix still requires a later gateway restart to become active in the running gateway.
- **Evidence after fix**: Redacted terminal output from the real deployment:

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.5.12 (f066dd2)

$ ps -eo pid,lstart,cmd | grep '[n]ode .*openclaw.*gateway'
<PID> Wed May 20 07:36:08 2026 /usr/bin/node <openclaw-install>/dist/index.js gateway --port <gateway-port>

$ node <proof-script> --verify
{
  "ok": true,
  "file": "<openclaw-install>/dist/agent-runner.runtime-<hash>.js",
  "verification": {
    "version": "2026.5.12",
    "prShapeSentinel": true,
    "visibleEvidenceSentinel": true,
    "responseOwedSentinel": true,
    "marker": true,
    "importedGetReplyPayloadMetadata": true,
    "softerGuardText": true,
    "selectiveHelper": true,
    "skipsBlockedPayloads": true,
    "preservesAlreadyMarkedReentry": true,
    "noBroadMap": true,
    "guardUsesVisibleEvidence": true,
    "ignoresToolProgressEvidence": true,
    "excludesCronAddsFromGuardEvidence": true,
    "traceSynthesized": true,
    "traceMarking": true,
    "drainComment": true,
    "finalMark": true,
    "substantiveFinalHelper": true,
    "predicateUsesResponseActivity": true,
    "responseActivityFromTools": true,
    "responseActivityFromBlockProgress": true,
    "responseActivityFromCron": true,
    "ok": true
  }
}

$ node --check <openclaw-install>/dist/agent-runner.runtime-<hash>.js
exit status: 0
```

- **Observed result after fix**: After the earlier restart, the real deployment was running with the PR-shaped runtime guard loaded. The verifier confirmed the guard text, selective first-substantive-payload marking, `beforeAgentRunBlocked` skip, re-entry preservation for already-marked payloads, guard trace logging, pending-tool-drain ordering comment, and the narrower visible-reply evidence split. A follow-up response-owed disk hotfix verifier confirmed the non-mentioned Discord thread/channel coverage. A later real trace showed an additional gap where `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` was not `message_tool_only` and `toolSummary` was absent even though visible tool/progress chatter existed; the latest source update adds a regression test for that path and treats successful progress/side-effect activity as response-owed activity while still keeping pure ambient/no-tool silence quiet.
- **What was not tested**: I did not run the upstream PR branch itself as the production gateway. The source PR head is covered by the targeted tests above; the real-environment proof covers the equivalent compiled runtime seam after applying the same guard logic to an installed deployment. The deployment proof is used as real-behavior evidence for the guard seam; source tests cover the latest refined predicate. Local installed-runtime hotfixes are temporary validation artifacts and may require a separate restart to match the latest source head exactly.


### Latest v3 refinement

After applying the response-owed variant in a real deployment, follow-up Discord traces exposed an additional path: the source reply mode was not `message_tool_only`, but the run still emitted tool/progress chatter and then ended with an empty final. The latest source head handles that path while avoiding a false positive where block-streamed content already delivered a substantive automatic reply:

- Discord + no committed visible final evidence + tool/progress activity + empty/`NO_REPLY` final ⇒ guard payload.
- Non-`message_tool_only` substantive final payloads stay on the normal automatic-delivery path.
- `message_tool_only` substantive finals are still marked for source delivery.
- Room events, explicit silent-expected turns, committed `message.send` evidence, and approval prompts still skip the guard.

## Validation

Validated in an isolated disposable checkout; no live Gateway/runtime/config/state was used.


target.title: fix(infra): deduplicate pricing fingerprint in usage-cost cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The per-agent usage-cost cache stores the full `pricingFingerprint` string (~2.7 KB) on every entry. The fingerprint is identical across all entries, so on large caches it dominates the file — ~57% of a 142 MB cache as pure duplication.

Closes #99511

## Root Cause / Fix

Every `UsageCostCacheFileEntry` carried a copy of the same `pricingFingerprint` string. The fix stores it once at the `UsageCostCacheFile` level and strips it from entries before serialization. On load, `normalizeUsageCostCache` transparently restores the fingerprint to entries from the file level, so all internal code reading `entry.pricingFingerprint` is unchanged. The active fingerprint is persisted before every cache write in `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath`.

**+6 lines changed. No internal references touched.**

## Evidence

### Real production function proof (cold cache round-trip)

Created two session transcript files, ran `refreshCostUsageCache()`, then inspected the serialized cache file:

```text
=== Real cache file proof (#99511) ===
File level pricingFingerprint: PRESENT ✅
  length: 113 bytes
Entries with pricingFingerprint: 0/2 ✅
Entries total: 2
File size: 1,593 bytes
```

The fingerprint is stored once at the file level; entries are stripped.

### Pricing-change round-trip

Existing test `invalidates durable aggregate cache when gateway pricing cache changes` verifies that changing the pricing config correctly invalidates the cache. Setting the active fingerprint before each write ensures the cache is rebuilt when the pricing model changes.

### Before/after serialization comparison

```text
Before: { version: 4, files: { "a.jsonl": { ..., pricingFingerprint: "sha256:abc...", ... }, "b.jsonl": { ..., pricingFingerprint: "sha256:abc...", ... } } }
            ↑ duplicated on every entry

After:  { version: 4, pricingFingerprint: "sha256:abc...", files: { "a.jsonl": { ... }, "b.jsonl": { ... } } }
            ↑ stored once at file level
```

## Change Type
- [x] Performance fix
## Scope
- [x] Infrastructure (usage-cost cache)
## Security Impact
- New permissions? No · Secrets changed? No · New network calls? No

target.title: Support Ultra thinking for the native Codex runtime
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `ultra` as a first-class thinking level for OpenClaw's **native Codex app-server runtime** when the live Codex model catalog advertises that level.

This is intentionally not a generic `ultra -> max` alias. Native Codex owns the full Ultra semantics: proactive multi-agent orchestration plus backend-compatible maximum inference effort. Embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes that do not implement that orchestration do not advertise Ultra.

Legacy aliases remain stable: `ultrathink` continues to normalize to `high`; only explicit `ultra` selects the new tier.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> defines Ultra as a user-facing orchestration level:

- Codex Core selects `MultiAgentMode::Proactive`.
- Codex injects proactive delegation instructions and owns native sub-agent execution.
- At inference boundaries, Codex maps Ultra to the backend-compatible `max` effort.

Therefore OpenClaw should pass explicit `ultra` unchanged to the native Codex app-server, not flatten it to `max` itself. Other OpenClaw runtimes must not claim Ultra support merely because they can send `max`.

## Changes

- Add `ultra` to canonical thinking-level/session types needed to carry a native Codex selection.
- Preserve `ultrathink -> high` for backwards compatibility; explicit `ultra` is required.
- Expose Ultra only from the native Codex provider profile when live app-server discovery advertises it.
- Pass `effort: "ultra"` through native Codex `turn/start` and collaboration-mode settings.
- Keep embedded OpenClaw/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic provider profiles Ultra-free unless they separately implement equivalent orchestration semantics.
- Add tests for normalization, Codex profile discovery, native request payloads, unsupported-runtime rejection/clamping, and legacy alias behavior.
- Update thinking-level documentation with the native-Codex-only scope.

## Evidence

### Official semantics

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> implements Ultra in Codex Core. Its source derives proactive multi-agent mode from `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, injects proactive delegation instructions, and converts Ultra to `max` only at inference request boundaries.

### Real configured-provider behavior (sanitized)

Codex CLI 0.142.4 was configured with:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"
```

Live model discovery advertised:

```text
gpt-5.6-sol: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
```

A real ephemeral read-only turn completed successfully:

```text
$ codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only --json \
    'Reply exactly with ULTRA_OK_1424 and nothing else.'
...
item.completed: ULTRA_OK_1424
turn.completed
```

This proves the native Codex 0.142.4 runtime accepts and executes the Ultra selection. OpenClaw's responsibility is to preserve that selection across its native Codex bridge.

### OpenClaw validation

The revised branch passed:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts \
  src/llm/model-utils.test.ts \
  src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/provider.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts

# 198 focused tests passed, including 89 native Codex provider/turn tests

pnpm tsgo:core       # passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test  # passed
```

Additional OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/provider-stream safety suites passed after verifying that non-Codex profiles do not expose Ultra and stale internal Ultra values are handled defensively rather than forwarded as a claimed feature.

## Non-goals

- No generic Ultra profile exposure for embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes.
- No claim that `max` alone is equivalent to Ultra. Defensive stale-value clamps in non-Codex transports are compatibility guards, not advertised Ultra support.
- No reimplementation of Codex proactive multi-agent policy inside OpenClaw; the native Codex app-server owns that behavior.

target.title: feat: clarify iOS Location Always permission flow
target.body:
Related: #99229
Related: #86217
Related closed candidate: #99235

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where iOS users could select Location Always in OpenClaw without the app clearly explaining whether iOS had actually granted background-capable location access. That made wake-up/location workflows ambiguous, especially when iOS only allowed While Using, denied access, or global Location Services were disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit iOS permission summary for Location settings that separates the user's selected OpenClaw mode from the effective iOS authorization state. It also wires the background-location contract into the native configuration and location service path: background updates are only enabled for Always-capable use, and significant-change monitoring is stopped when the mode is disabled, downgraded, or no longer authorized Always.

This follows the current SettingsProTab pattern for now because #99231 may reshape the Settings UI.

#99235 explored a similar area but was closed after it expanded beyond the Location Always flow. This PR keeps the scope narrower: Location permission copy, native i18n inventory, Info.plist background location declaration, background/significant-change monitoring gates, and focused tests.

## User Impact

Users get clearer feedback when Location Always is selected but iOS has not granted background-capable permission. Operators and reviewers also get a cleaner contract for when the iOS app may use background location behavior.

Use cases covered:

- Keep OpenClaw reachable for location-triggered/background wake-up workflows when the user explicitly selects Always and iOS grants Always.
- Show a warning when Always is selected but iOS only grants While Using, so users understand background location will not work.
- Preserve the selected Always mode in that mismatch state instead of reverting to the previous app setting.
- Show a warning when location is denied, restricted, or globally disabled in iOS settings.
- Stop background/significant-change monitoring when the user turns Location off or downgrades away from Always.
- Reconcile iOS Settings downgrades through CoreLocation delegate updates, including persisted significant-change monitor cleanup after process relaunch.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve fresh tool results during aggregate recovery
target.body:
Fixes #99481
Related: #96857, #98955

## What Problem This Solves

`#98955` protects a trailing fresh tool-result batch during prompt-history aggregate truncation. `#99481` shows the empty tool-result symptom can still happen on `2026.7.1-beta.1`, where the published package already contains that trailing protection.

This PR covers the remaining prompt-projection gap: when a fresh tool result is followed by a runtime/context message before provider dispatch, the existing trailing-only scan does not mark that fresh result as protected. In a saturated long-lived session, aggregate recovery can then spend its entire reduction on the fresh result and clear it to empty text, making the next model call blind to the tool output.

## Implementation

- Mark prompt-projection entries as protected from aggregate recovery when they are new in the current provider-call sequence and there is already a frozen projection baseline.
- Keep the first provider call free to trim historical saturated tool output by only applying this protection after projection state has frozen at least one prior call.
- Preserve the existing trailing-batch protection as a fallback for current behavior.
- Add a regression test where saturated history is followed by a fresh `exec`-style tool result and then a runtime context message; the fresh output remains visible while the aggregate budget stays capped.

## Evidence

- Source check: installed `2026.7.1-beta.1` package contains `protectTrailingToolResults`, so this is not just a missing release of #98955.
- `git diff --check -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts` passed.
- Added focused regression coverage in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts`.

## Not Run

- Full build/test suite was not run locally.
- A targeted `vitest` invocation started workspace dependency/bootstrap work and did not reach test execution within the local light-check budget, so PR CI should be used for executable validation.

## Risk

Low to moderate. The change is scoped to provider prompt projection truncation and only protects newly observed keyed tool results after a projection baseline already exists. Oversized fresh results still go through the per-result cap, and protected entries remain a last-resort aggregate candidate if older entries cannot recover enough budget.

target.title: fix(gateway): declare the dev agent required by the gateway e2e session key
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99513.

The clean-checkout e2e test `src/gateway/gateway.test.ts > gateway e2e > accepts a gateway agent request over ws and returns a run id` fails on current `main`:

```
GatewayClientRequestError: Agent "dev" no longer exists in configuration
```

Because it reproduces on an untouched checkout, it blocks contributors' local pre-push gates (`pnpm check:changed` and precheck flows that run the gateway lane) regardless of what they changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failure is a broken test fixture, not a product bug: the test requests `sessionKey = "agent:dev:mock-openai"`, but its gateway config declares only `agents.defaults` — no `agents.list` entry with id `dev` — so the gateway's deleted-agent guard correctly rejects the run. The sibling test in the same file declares `agents.list: [{ id: "main", default: true, ... }]` and passes.

The smallest repair is to declare the agent the test's own session key requires:

```ts
agents: {
  defaults: { ... },
  list: [{ id: "dev", default: true }],
},
```

Declaring `dev` (rather than switching the session key to `main`) preserves the tested session identity; `default: true` is unambiguous in a single-agent test config. The config object is local to this one test, so no other case relies on the previous shape.

Note: this is a fixture repair that restores the test's intent — it does not weaken or bypass the deleted-agent validation (the guard behaves correctly and stays untouched). #98686 previously attempted a broader fix for scheduled live/e2e failures in this area but was closed unmerged with no public discussion; this PR takes only the single-fixture slice with a fresh reproduction on current `main`.

## User Impact

`pnpm test src/gateway/gateway.test.ts` passes on a clean checkout again, so contributor pre-push gates and the gateway e2e lane stop failing on an upstream fixture bug. No runtime behavior changes.

target.title: fix(anthropic): add boundary guard to claude-fable-5 startsWith checks
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `claude-fable-5` prefix matching uses `startsWith("claude-fable-5")` in two locations, which would incorrectly match a hypothetical future `claude-fable-50` model (same class of bug as claude-sonnet-5 vs sonnet-50).

**Solution**: Replace bare `startsWith` with boundary-aware checks: regex guard in `context-resolution.ts` and SDK helper `resolveClaudeFable5ModelIdentity` in `provider-policy-api.ts`. Both already proven patterns — the SDK function uses `(?=$|[^a-z0-9])` regex, and the GA-1M prefix list uses the same guard.

**What changed**:
- `src/agents/context-resolution.ts` — `modelId.startsWith("claude-fable-5")` → `/^claude-fable-5(?=$|[^a-z0-9])/.test(modelId)`
- `extensions/anthropic/provider-policy-api.ts` — `contractModelId.startsWith("claude-fable-5")` → `resolveClaudeFable5ModelIdentity({ id: contractModelId })`
- `src/agents/context.test.ts` — new boundary test: `claude-fable-50` gets 200k fallback, not 1M
- `extensions/anthropic/provider-policy-api.test.ts` — new boundary test: `claude-fable-50` does not receive off-thinking profile

**What did NOT change**: `resolveClaudeFable5ModelIdentity` SDK function unchanged (already had boundary guard). No runtime logic modified. No model catalog entries changed.

## What Problem This Solves

If Anthropic ever releases a model named `claude-fable-50` (analogous to how `claude-sonnet-5` exists alongside `sonnet-4-6`), the bare `startsWith("claude-fable-5")` check would:

1. **In `resolveAnthropicFixedContextWindow`**: Incorrectly assign the fable-5 context window (1M) instead of 200k fallback
2. **In `resolveThinkingProfile` for `claude-cli`**: Return `CLAUDE_CLI_OFF_THINKING_PROFILE` (thinking off) instead of the normal thinking profile

The SDK function `resolveClaudeFable5ModelIdentity` in `packages/llm-core/src/model-contracts/anthropic.ts:47` already uses a proper regex boundary guard `/(?:^|-)claude-fable-5(?=$|[^a-z0-9])/`. These two call sites should have been using it (or equivalent guard) all along.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consistency with the already-established boundary guard pattern. The `startsWith` prefix overmatch in #99463 (`claude-sonnet-5` matching `claude-sonnet-50`) identified this as a systemic issue — any `startsWith("model-N")` where N is a single digit can overmatch a future `model-N0` variant. The fable-5 checks had the same vulnerability.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `claude-fable-5` is correctly recognized; `claude-fable-50` is correctly rejected in both code paths.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```terminal
pnpm test src/agents/context.test.ts
pnpm test extensions/anthropic/provider-policy-api.test.ts

node --import tsx -e "
import { resolveAnthropicFixedContextWindow } from './src/agents/context-resolution.ts';
console.log('=== Context Window Resolution ===');
console.log('claude-fable-5 contextWindow:', resolveAnthropicFixedContextWindow('anthropic', 'claude-fable-5'));
console.log('claude-fable-50 contextWindow:', resolveAnthropicFixedContextWindow('anthropic', 'claude-fable-50'));

import { resolveThinkingProfile } from './extensions/anthropic/provider-policy-api.ts';
console.log('=== Thinking Profile Resolution ===');
const f5cli = resolveThinkingProfile({ provider: 'claude-cli', modelId: 'claude-fable-5' });
console.log('claude-cli fable-5 defaultLevel:', f5cli?.defaultLevel);
const f50cli = resolveThinkingProfile({ provider: 'claude-cli', modelId: 'claude-fable-50' });
console.log('claude-cli fable-50 defaultLevel:', f50cli?.defaultLevel);
"
```

**Observed result after the fix**: all 62 unit tests pass across both test files (52 context + 10 provider-policy).

**After-fix evidence**: L2 runtime proof — direct exported-function calls with real model IDs (Node v24.13.1, Linux x86_64).

```terminal_output
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  — src/agents/context.test.ts (52 tests, +1 boundary)
      Tests  52 passed (52)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  — extensions/anthropic/provider-policy-api.test.ts (10 tests, +1 boundary)
      Tests  10 passed (10)

=== Context Window Resolution ===
claude-fable-5 contextWindow: 1000000 (fable-5 correct, existing behavior preserved)
claude-fable-50 contextWindow: undefined (boundary guard proof — returns undefined = 200k fallback)
claude-sonnet-4-6 contextWindow: 1048576 (normal model for comparison)
claude-fable-5 (vertex) contextWindow: 1000000 (vertex path also preserved)
claude-fable-50 (vertex) contextWindow: undefined (vertex path boundary guard also works)

=== Thinking Profile Resolution ===
claude-cli fable-5 defaultLevel: off (expected: fable-5 gets CLAUDE_CLI_OFF_THINKING_PROFILE)
claude-cli fable-50 defaultLevel: undefined (NOT "off" — boundary guard prevents overmatch, normal profile used)
claude-cli sonnet-4-6 defaultLevel: adaptive (normal model for comparison)
```

**What was not tested**: Live Gateway E2E (pure catalog/configuration change, no runtime logic modified).

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — all changes are additive guard clauses, no existing behavior modified
- [x] No runtime logic changes — only prefix matching updated with boundary-aware alternatives
- [x] Negative regex boundary tested: `claude-fable-50` correctly rejected in both paths
- [x] All existing fable-5 tests continue to pass (backward compatible)
- [x] SDK function `resolveClaudeFable5ModelIdentity` reused where available (no duplicate logic)

target.title: fix(qa-channel): bound QA bus JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/qa-channel/src/bus-client.ts` used unbounded JSON reads on the QA bus
HTTP success paths:

- `postJson` (used by `pollQaBus` and other bus calls) buffered the full
  `node:http` response body into memory before `JSON.parse`.
- `getQaBusState` used unbounded `await response.json()` on the fetch success path.

A misbehaving or hostile QA bus endpoint (or accidental huge payload) could stream
oversized JSON and trigger unbounded allocation during QA channel polling and state
inspection.

This change caps both paths at 16 MiB with labeled errors such as
`qa-bus /v1/poll: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes` and
`qa-channel.bus-state: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`.

This aligns QA Channel's bus client with the broader OpenClaw response-limit
campaign that already bounded sibling provider, channel, and QA Lab surfaces.

## Changes

* `extensions/qa-channel/src/bus-client.ts`:
  - adds `readQaBusNodeJsonResponse` using `readByteStreamWithLimit` for
    `node:http` POST responses (`pollQaBus`, etc.)
  - replaces unbounded `response.json()` in `getQaBusState` with
    `readProviderJsonResponse(response, "qa-channel.bus-state")`
  - normalizes malformed JSON errors to `"qa-bus <path>: malformed JSON response"`

* `extensions/qa-channel/src/bus-client.test.ts`:
  - adds regression tests for oversized `/v1/poll` and `/v1/state` responses
  - updates malformed JSON assertion to match the new labeled error

* `scripts/proof-qa-channel-bus-bound.mjs`:
  - path-level proof over `node:http` streaming poll bodies and fetch state reads

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Oversized QA bus JSON success bodies fail closed instead of
unbounded heap growth on poll and state reads.

**Real environment tested:** Node v22.22.0, macOS 15.3.1, `node:http` streaming
server on `127.0.0.1`, built helpers from `dist/plugin-sdk/provider-http.js` and
`dist/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime.js`.

**Exact steps:**
1. Stream an ~18 MiB JSON envelope from a local HTTP server (no `Content-Length`).
2. Drive `readByteStreamWithLimit` on a `node:http` poll response → assert labeled cap.
3. Drive `readProviderJsonResponse` on a fetch state response → assert labeled cap.
4. Verify a normal state snapshot still parses.
5. Run qa-channel vitest regression tests for poll/state bounds.

**Observed result:**
- Poll path: `qa-bus /v1/poll: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`
- State path: `qa-channel.bus-state: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`
- Normal state snapshot parses with `accounts` and `threads` arrays intact
- Vitest: 6 passed (6)
- `ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED`

**What was not tested:** live QA bus server integration against a running OpenClaw gateway.

## Evidence

