target.title: feat(whatsapp): add replyToOfflineMessages config to process missed messages after reconnect
target.body:
## Problem

Messages received during WhatsApp disconnects are **silently lost**. When the gateway reconnects, offline messages arrive with `upsert.type === "append"` (history sync) and are **skipped** by default.

This causes:
- DM messages lost after reconnect
- Group messages stop working after gateway restart
- Blue ticks sent but no reply (sender sees message read but ignored)

**15+ issues** trace back to the same `append` skip.

## Solution

Add opt-in config to process offline messages:

```json5
{
  channels: {
    whatsapp: {
      replyToOfflineMessages: true,
      offlineMessageMaxAgeSeconds: 300, // default: 300 (5 minutes)
    },
  },
}
```

- `replyToOfflineMessages: true` — Process offline messages instead of skipping
- `offlineMessageMaxAgeSeconds: 300` — Skip messages older than 5 minutes (prevent flooding)

## Related Issues

- **#50093** — WhatsApp: Backfill missed messages after reconnection
- **#66904** — Support WhatsApp history sync on reconnect (closed as duplicate)
- **#19856** — Messages lost after 408 reconnect
- **#1619** — Messages lost during disconnect
- **#18672** — Messages dropped after prekey renegotiation
- **#1952, #2767, #20952** — Group messages stop after restart
- **#14069** — Group messages stop after relinking

## Based On

This PR is based on **#21719** by @faahim which was closed by stale bot due to inactivity.

The original PR had:
- ✅ Complete solution
- ✅ Tests passing
- ✅ Docs updated
- ✅ 15+ issues identified

## Changes

1. `src/config/types.whatsapp.ts` — Add config fields
2. `extensions/whatsapp/src/accounts.ts` — Add resolved fields
3. `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/monitor.ts` — Implement logic
4. `extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor.ts` — Pass options

## Default Behavior

**Unchanged** — By default, offline messages are still skipped (`replyToOfflineMessages: false`). Users must opt-in to process them.

---

**Context:** OpenClaw WhatsApp bundled user since 2026.3.13, currently on latest version.

target.title: feat(hooks): add persistent hook session mode
target.body:
## Summary Revives the persistent hook-session work from the stale/closed #27193 against current `main`. Adds an explicit `sessionMode: "isolated" | "persistent"` option for hook-agent runs so webhook integrations with stable, scoped `sessionKey` values can opt into multi-turn transcript reuse. Fixes #11665. ## Why Current hook-agent dispatch still routes direct `/hooks/agent` calls and mapped hook actions through the isolated cron-style runner. Even when callers provide the same `sessionKey`, that path passes `forceNew: true`, so OpenClaw creates a fresh session id and loses conversation history on every webhook invocation. Issue #11665 now spells out essentially the same narrow fix as #27193: keep the existing default isolation, but expose an explicit persistent mode for trusted hook threads. We have also been running this behavior in production for months on our shel-oodle OpenClaw instance. That production branch carried the same `sessionMode` behavior while tracking upstream releases, including the later hooks request-handler refactor. ## What changed - Adds `sessionMode` to hook mapping config/types/schema and generated config metadata. - Accepts `sessionMode` on direct `/hooks/agent` payloads. - Threads `sessionMode` through mapping resolution, transform results, replay dedupe scope, and hook dispatch. - Changes `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` so only explicit `sessionMode: "persistent"` hook-agent runs avoid `forceNew` and can reuse a fresh stored session id. - Documents the security model: `isolated` remains the default; persistent mode should only be used with trusted integrations and scoped `sessionKey` values. Existing request `sessionKey` and prefix policy checks are unchanged. ## Compatibility / security - Default behavior is unchanged: omitted `sessionMode` behaves as `"isolated"` and creates a fresh session per hook dispatch. - Cron isolation remains unchanged unless the hook dispatch explicitly passes `sessionMode: "persistent"`. - Existing `hooks.allowRequestSessionKey` and `hooks.allowedSessionKeyPrefixes` checks still gate externally supplied or templated session keys. - Idempotency replay scope includes `sessionMode`, so different lifecycle modes are not conflated. ## Variance from #11665 spec None known. This implements the requested `sessionMode: "isolated" | "persistent"` surface for direct `/hooks/agent`, hook mappings, and transform results while preserving default isolation. ## Real behavior proof - **Behavior or issue addressed:** Hook-agent dispatch now supports explicit persistent hook sessions while preserving isolated default behavior. - **Real environment tested:** Live `shel-oodle-1` OpenClaw gateway, running `v2026.6.1` from this PR branch at `e4bce7737e128e72655a4c388a4ebed66e3b2053`. This proof used a real Fizzy webhook integration, real gateway/proxy services, a real persistent hook mapping, the real stored OpenClaw session store, and a real `gpt-5.5` Codex harness run. Secrets, account ids, SGIDs, and nonessential user/account fields are redacted below. - **Live services during proof:** ```console openclaw-gateway.service active (running) fizzy-webhook.service active (running) cloudflared.service active (running) Gateway version: OpenClaw 2026.6.1 (e4bce77) ``` - **Live webhook delivery proof:** A real Fizzy Playground card (`#1217`) generated real webhook events. The local Fizzy proxy accepted the signed events and forwarded them to the OpenClaw gateway with HTTP 200. ```console Jun 05 01:59:11 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T05:59:11.836Z] info: Fizzy webhook: card_published Jun 05 01:59:11 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T05:59:11.874Z] info: Forwarded to gateway: 200 Jun 05 02:00:10 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T06:00:10.288Z] info: Fizzy webhook: comment_created Jun 05 02:00:10 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T06:00:10.436Z] info: Forwarded to gateway: 200 Jun 05 02:00:35 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T06:00:35.329Z] info: Fizzy webhook: comment_created Jun 05 02:00:35 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T06:00:35.482Z] info: Forwarded to gateway: 200 Jun 05 02:00:50 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T06:00:50.276Z] info: Fizzy webhook: comment_created Jun 05 02:00:50 shel-oodle node[25078]: [2026-06-05T06:00:50.417Z] info: Forwarded to gateway: 200 ``` - **Persistent session reuse proof:** The same stable hook `sessionKey` reused the same stored OpenClaw `sessionId` and native Codex `threadId` across separate webhook invocations for card `#1217`. ```console # first live webhook turn, card_created/card_published type=session.started ts=2026-06-05T05:59:15.128Z sessionId=b99c7c98-2271-4af9-96f3-8f8a1bc4113a sessionKey=agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 threadId=019e965d-439c-7821-93c5-73f4e521e2ee provider=openai modelId=gpt-5.5 # later live webhook turn, user comment/@mention type=session.started ts=2026-06-05T06:00:36.552Z sessionId=b99c7c98-2271-4af9-96f3-8f8a1bc4113a sessionKey=agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 threadId=019e965d-439c-7821-93c5-73f4e521e2ee provider=openai modelId=gpt-5.5 # follow-up webhook generated by Sheldon's own Fizzy comment type=session.started ts=2026-06-05T06:00:53.300Z sessionId=b99c7c98-2271-4af9-96f3-8f8a1bc4113a sessionKey=agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 threadId=019e965d-439c-7821-93c5-73f4e521e2ee provider=openai modelId=gpt-5.5 ``` - **Real model/tool execution proof:** The first live turn reached the model and attempted the requested card-context command. It failed because the deployed environment did not have the helper command on `PATH`; this is useful proof that the persistent hook session reached real agent/tool execution rather than a mocked runner. ```console type=tool.call ts=2026-06-05T05:59:25.483Z sessionId=b99c7c98-2271-4af9-96f3-8f8a1bc4113a sessionKey=agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 provider=openai modelId=gpt-5.5 command=/bin/bash -lc 'fizzy-context 1217' type=tool.result ts=2026-06-05T05:59:25.500Z status=failed exitCode=127 output=/bin/bash: line 1: fizzy-context: command not found ``` - **Real same-thread response proof:** A later real comment webhook reused the same persistent session and the agent posted back to the same Fizzy card thread. The command output below is redacted to remove account/user ids and SGIDs while preserving the behavior evidence. ```console type=tool.call ts=2026-06-05T06:00:50.086Z sessionId=b99c7c98-2271-4af9-96f3-8f8a1bc4113a sessionKey=agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 provider=openai modelId=gpt-5.5 command=fizzy comment create --card 1217 --body '

[redacted mention] Confirmed, I received the reply on card #1217 and am posting back into the same Fizzy thread.

' type=tool.result ts=2026-06-05T06:00:50.328Z status=completed exitCode=0 output={"success":true,"data":{"body":{"plain_text":"[redacted mention] Confirmed, I received the reply on card #1217 and am posting back into the same Fizzy thread."},"card":{"url":"https://app.fizzy.do/[redacted]/cards/1217"},"creator":{"name":"Sheldon"},"url":"https://app.fizzy.do/[redacted]/cards/1217/comments/[redacted]"}} ``` - **Gateway lifecycle proof:** The gateway ran the live hook agent with the expected provider/model after the config repair and reported successful completion for the later persistent hook turns. ```console Jun 05 02:00:13 shel-oodle node[554078]: [diagnostic] lane wait exceeded: lane=session:agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 waitedMs=3223 queueAhead=0 activeAhead=1 activeNow=0 queueBehind=0 Jun 05 02:00:13 shel-oodle node[554078]: [agent/embedded] selected agent harness: provider=openai model=gpt-5.5 harness=codex requested=- runtimeOverride=- Jun 05 02:00:14 shel-oodle node[554078]: [diagnostic] message processed: channel=cron chatId=unknown messageId=unknown sessionId=b99c7c98-2271-4af9-96f3-8f8a1bc4113a sessionKey=agent:fizzy-orchestrator:hook:fizzy:card-1217 outcome=error duration=59941ms error="fizzy-context 1217 failed" Jun 05 02:00:17 shel-oodle node[554078]: [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement Jun 05 02:00:52 shel-oodle node[554078]: [agent/embedded] selected agent harness: provider=openai model=gpt-5.5 harness=codex requested=- runtimeOverride=- Jun 05 02:00:53 shel-oodle node[554078]: [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement Jun 05 02:00:55 shel-oodle node[554078]: [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement ``` - **Default isolated proof:** The live proof above covers explicit persistent hook reuse in a real setup. Default omitted/isolated behavior remains covered by targeted tests that assert `forceNew: true` and distinct run-scoped session keys for repeated default isolated runs. ```console stdout | ../../src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-key-isolation.test.ts > runCronIsolatedAgentTurn isolated session identity > uses a run-scoped key for embedded isolated cron execution [diagnostic] message queued: sessionId=isolated-run-1 sessionKey=agent:default:cron:daily-monitor:run:isolated-run-1 source=cron-isolated queueDepth=1 sessionState=idle [diagnostic] message processed: channel=cron chatId=unknown messageId=unknown sessionId=isolated-run-1 sessionKey=agent:default:cron:daily-monitor:run:isolated-run-1 outcome=completed duration=244ms stdout | ../../src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-key-isolation.test.ts > runCronIsolatedAgentTurn isolated session identity > keeps embedded isolated cron prompt-cache affinity stable across run sessions [diagnostic] message queued: sessionId=isolated-run-a sessionKey=agent:default:cron:daily-monitor:run:isolated-run-a source=cron-isolated queueDepth=1 sessionState=idle [diagnostic] message queued: sessionId=isolated-run-b sessionKey=agent:default:cron:daily-monitor:run:isolated-run-b source=cron-isolated queueDepth=1 sessionState=idle ✓ |cron| ../../src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-key-isolation.test.ts > runCronIsolatedAgentTurn isolated session identity > uses a run-scoped key for embedded isolated cron execution 476ms ✓ |cron| ../../src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-key-isolation.test.ts > runCronIsolatedAgentTurn isolated session identity > keeps embedded isolated cron prompt-cache affinity stable across run sessions 137ms ``` - **Observed result after fix:** Persistent hook mode reused the same real stored session and native Codex thread across multiple real webhook deliveries, and a later hook turn posted a real same-card Fizzy comment. Default isolated behavior remains covered by focused regression tests. ## Testing Passed locally after the latest rebase/update: - `node scripts/pre-commit/pnpm-audit-prod.mjs --audit-level=high && pnpm config:schema:check && pnpm config:docs:check && pnpm test src/config/config-misc.test.ts src/gateway/hooks-mapping.test.ts src/gateway/hooks.test.ts src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-key-isolation.test.ts && pnpm build` - `pnpm test src/gateway/hooks.test.ts src/gateway/hooks-mapping.test.ts src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/session.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.session-key-isolation.test.ts` - `pnpm test src/config/config-misc.test.ts` - `pnpm config:docs:gen` - `pnpm config:schema:check` - `pnpm config:docs:check` - `pnpm check:changed` - `pnpm build` I did not run the full monorepo test suite; this is a large workspace, and the targeted acceptance tests plus changed-file gate/build cover the hook/config/cron surfaces touched here. ## Prior art - Replaces/revives stale closed PR #27193 with a fresh current-main branch. - Related issue: #11665.

target.title: fix(googlechat): preserve unresolved service account refs
target.body:
## Summary
- Preserve unresolved Google Chat `serviceAccountRef` as an error instead of silently falling back to legacy inline `serviceAccount` credentials.
- Add regression coverage for mixed `serviceAccountRef` + inline `serviceAccount` config.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Google Chat credential resolution must honor documented SecretRef precedence. A config with both `serviceAccountRef` and inline `serviceAccount` must fail closed when the ref is unresolved, and a resolved runtime snapshot must remove the sibling ref before Google Chat reads credentials.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw PR worktree on the rebased head `ef2bfcd48f`, using Node/pnpm from the repo environment. I checked env and `~/.profile` for Google Chat service-account material without printing values; none was present, so this uses redacted service-account JSON through the production Google Chat account resolver plus runtime SecretRef assignment/resolution paths.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran `pnpm exec tsx` against `extensions/googlechat/src/accounts.ts` and `extensions/googlechat/src/secret-contract.ts`, invoking `resolveGoogleChatAccount`, `collectRuntimeConfigAssignments`, `resolveSecretRefValues`, and `applyResolvedAssignments` with a mixed ref-plus-inline Google Chat config and a resolved env SecretRef snapshot.

**Evidence after fix:** Redacted terminal output from the production-path proof command:

```text
real-behavior-proof: googlechat SecretRef precedence
credential availability check: no GOOGLE_CHAT_* service-account env/profile entries were present; proof uses redacted service-account JSON through production resolver paths
mixed ref-plus-inline: FAIL_CLOSED
mixed ref-plus-inline error: channels.googlechat.accounts.default.serviceAccount: unresolved SecretRef "file:filemain:/channels/googlechat/missing-service-account". Resolve this command against an active gateway runtime snapshot before reading it.
mixed ref-plus-inline inline fallback used: false
resolved snapshot assignments: channels.googlechat.accounts.prod.serviceAccount
resolved snapshot warnings: SECRETS_REF_OVERRIDES_PLAINTEXT
resolved snapshot serviceAccountRef removed: true
resolved snapshot account source: inline
resolved snapshot client_email: REDACTED@redacted-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
resolved snapshot private_key: REDACTED
resolved snapshot inline legacy used: false
```

**Observed result after fix:** The stale mixed `serviceAccountRef` plus inline `serviceAccount` case failed closed before inline fallback, and the resolved snapshot path produced an account with the redacted resolved service-account email, removed `serviceAccountRef`, and did not use the legacy inline email.

**What was not tested:** A live Google Chat API send/webhook with real service-account credentials was not tested because this machine did not expose Google Chat credentials. The exercised paths are the production Google Chat credential resolver and runtime SecretRef resolver, not mocked test-only helpers.

## Maintainer compatibility note
This intentionally keeps the documented fail-closed precedence: when `serviceAccountRef` is present but unresolved, Google Chat does not fall back to inline `serviceAccount`, even if the inline credentials are otherwise valid. Existing stale mixed configs must repair/remove the stale ref or resolve it successfully.

## Tests
- `pnpm test extensions/googlechat/src/setup.test.ts extensions/googlechat/src/secret-contract.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 CHANGELOG.md extensions/googlechat/src/accounts.ts extensions/googlechat/src/secret-contract.test.ts extensions/googlechat/src/secret-contract.ts extensions/googlechat/src/setup.test.ts`
- `pnpm changed:lanes --json`
- `pnpm check:changed`

target.title: fix(agents): pause yielded main-session runs
target.body:
## Summary

Extend the subagent yield-pause fix from [6f3b5f86](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6f3b5f8666f3a3877b62d9019b8842455fdf62e1) to top-level (non-subagent) sessions.

When a main session ends via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner already emits a lifecycle event with `yielded: true` and `livenessState: "paused"`. The runner's terminal lifecycle metadata, the agent-job snapshot cache, and the agent.wait dedupe entry all propagate those flags generically, so subagent and non-subagent runs benefit equally from those parts of 6f3b5f86.

The gap is in `gateway/session-lifecycle-state.ts`. `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` does not look at the `yielded` flag, so the session entry is persisted with `status: \"done\"` even though the runner has queued a post-yield continuation that drains on the next turn. Dashboards, restart recovery, and follow-up turns then treat the session as finished and race the continuation, producing the in-context overflow and out-of-order events the user reports.

## Why the same fix needs to apply to the top-level session

The subagent registry tracks active subagent runs in memory and uses `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` to keep yielded entries in a paused state instead of marking them complete. The main session has no equivalent in-memory registry; its lifecycle state is persisted directly through `persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` into the on-disk session entry. The gap shows up in three places:

1. The persisted session entry says `status: \"done\"`, so `sessions_list`, `sessions.changed` broadcasts, and dashboard UI all show the session as finished.
2. `main-session-restart-recovery` is keyed off `entry.abortedLastRun` and `entry.status === \"running\"`. With status=done it leaves the entry alone, but on a clean restart-mid-yield the yielded session can also end up `abortedLastRun=true` (the cleaned-lock path), at which point recovery would force a `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted...` resume that races the queued continuation.
3. A new user message arrives at a session that is internally paused but externally \"done\" — the gateway dispatches a fresh agent.run, and the queued steered yield-interrupt drains alongside the new user input, producing out-of-order assistant text.

## Shape of the change

- Recognize the lifecycle `yielded` flag in `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` and derive `status: \"paused\"` with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` instead of `done`. Yielded short-circuits before the `aborted`/`stopReason` branches so partial classifications cannot mask the paused state.
- Clear `pauseReason` on the next lifecycle `start` event so a fresh run reactivates the session, mirroring how `subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` clears `pauseReason` on completion.
- Add `\"paused\"` to `SessionRunStatus` in both `gateway/session-utils.types.ts` and `agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts`, and add `pauseReason?: \"sessions_yield\"` to `SessionEntry` and `GatewaySessionRow`.
- Surface `pauseReason` on the `sessions.changed` broadcast snapshot and the `loadGatewaySessionRow` builder so consumers (UI, sessions_list tool) see the paused state.
- Tighten `isTerminalSessionStatus` so the type predicate stays accurate after \"paused\" joins the union (paused is not terminal).
- Skip `main-session-restart-recovery` for entries with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` so they are not re-prompted with the generic interrupted-turn message.

The runner-level changes (yieldDetected -> livenessState=paused/yielded=true) and the gateway agent-job/agent-wait-dedupe propagation that 6f3b5f86 already added are unchanged. This PR plugs the missing seam between those generic signals and the persisted session entry.

## Test coverage

- `src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts`:
  - `marks yielded lifecycle end events as paused with sessions_yield reason` (persisted patch).
  - `treats yielded as paused even when aborted is set` (yield short-circuit).
  - `clears pauseReason when a fresh run starts on a paused session` (start-phase reactivation).
  - Existing terminal-mapping tests updated to include explicit `pauseReason: undefined` on non-yield ends.
- `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts`:
  - `skips sessions paused via sessions_yield instead of forcing a resume`.
  - `does not mark sessions with sessions_yield pauseReason as restart-aborted from cleaned locks`.

## Local validation

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts src/config/sessions.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.create-event.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent-wait-dedupe.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-output.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — all green (235 tests).
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm check:changelog-attributions` — all clean on changed files.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on \`fix(agents): pause yielded main-session runs\`.
- [ ] Manual smoke: trigger `sessions_yield` from a main-session conversation; confirm the session entry persists `status: paused` and `pauseReason: sessions_yield`, and that a follow-up turn flips back to `running` with `pauseReason: undefined`.
- [ ] Restart-recovery smoke: kill the gateway while a main session is paused via yield; confirm restart-recovery skips it instead of re-prompting with the interrupted-turn message.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Before this PR, when a top-level (non-subagent) embedded `openclaw` run ended via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner emitted `yielded=true` and `livenessState=paused` but the gateway treated it as a clean completion and wrote `status=done`. The session displayed as finished while awaiting a queued post-yield continuation, racing dashboards, restart-recovery, and follow-up turns. After this PR, the lifecycle persistence derives `status=paused` with `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, restart-recovery skips paused sessions, and `SessionRunStatus` adds `"paused"` so consumers can distinguish a yielded run from a completed one.
- **Real environment tested**: live OpenClaw gateway on rh-bot.lan, pid 65734, build SHA 23804e610c (upgrade-v2026.5.28 with this PR cherry-picked). The deployed `dist/server-chat-*.js` and `dist/main-session-restart-recovery-*.js` chunks carry the new `pauseReason`/`sessions_yield` logic; the proof script imports and executes those exact bundle bytes.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  # On rh-bot.lan, confirm deployed bundles carry the PR logic:
  grep -c 'sessions_yield\|pauseReason' \
    /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js
  # -> 1 (the new shouldSkipMainRecovery branch)

  grep -c 'sessions_yield\|pauseReason' \
    /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js
  # -> non-zero (new deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot branches)

  # Drive the deployed code with three scenarios:
  node /tmp/proof-75662-amittell.mjs
  ```
  Proof script (`/tmp/proof-75662-amittell.mjs`) extracts the deployed
  `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` from `server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js` via
  `vm.runInContext`, dynamically imports `main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js`
  to grab the exported `markRestartAbortedMainSessions`, seeds a temp
  state-dir with one yielded and one non-yielded `running` entry, and asserts
  three behaviors:
  1. Lifecycle `phase=end` with `yielded=true` -> `status=paused`,
     `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, `abortedLastRun=false`.
  2. Same entry passed to restart-recovery is SKIPPED (no `abortedLastRun`
     write, `updatedAt` unchanged).
  3. Sibling running entry without `pauseReason` is marked
     `abortedLastRun=true` (existing behavior preserved).
  Plus a guard check: lifecycle `phase=error` with `yielded=true` returns
  `status=failed` with NO `pauseReason` leak.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  === PR #75662 real-behavior proof ===
  host=rh-bot.lan pid=84884 node=v25.8.2
  dist=/Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist

  [1] lifecycle bundle: /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js
  [1a] yielded terminal -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"paused","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false,"pauseReason":"sessions_yield"}
  [1a] OK: paused status carries pauseReason=sessions_yield
  [1b] non-yielded terminal -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"done","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false}
  [1b] OK: non-yielded run preserves status=done with no pauseReason
  [1c] error+yielded -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"failed","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false}
  [1c] OK: error phase masks yielded marker, no pauseReason leak

  [2] seeded /var/folders/cn/.../state/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
  [2] recovery bundle: /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js
  [2] exports: i, n, r, t
  [main-session-restart-recovery] marked 1 interrupted main session(s) for restart recovery (pr-75662-proof)
  [2] mark result: {"marked":1,"skipped":1}
  [2] yielded entry after: {"sessionId":"sess-yielded","status":"running","pauseReason":"sessions_yield","startedAt":...,"updatedAt":1780285519789}
  [2] normal entry after:  {"sessionId":"sess-normal","status":"running","startedAt":...,"updatedAt":1780285521266,"abortedLastRun":true}
  [2a] OK: yielded session was skipped (no abortedLastRun, no updatedAt bump)
  [2b] OK: non-yielded running session was marked abortedLastRun=true

  === ALL PROOFS PASSED ===
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: All three scenarios pass on the deployed bundle. A yielded terminal event produces `status=paused`/`pauseReason=sessions_yield` and is skipped by restart recovery (no `abortedLastRun` mutation, no `updatedAt` bump). A non-yielded terminal event still produces `status=done` with no `pauseReason` (existing behavior preserved). An error phase masks the `yielded` flag and reports `status=failed` with no `pauseReason` leak, matching the gating comment in `resolveTerminalStatus`.
- **Targeted tests**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts` -> 22 passed + 15 passed (37/37). Broader: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts` -> 172/172 passed. `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --only=core --threads=4` -> clean.
- **What was not tested**: End-to-end live channel trigger (sending a real Telegram message that drives `sessions_yield` to completion); this is exercised by the existing vitest coverage in `pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` rather than reproduced live on rh-bot.


## Live exact-head capture (2026-06-12): found and fixed an emit-side gap

Running the requested live scenario on an isolated sandbox gateway (loopback :28795, fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, Control UI webchat, native `openai-completions` lane with a tool-calling model) surfaced a real defect in this PR's original head: **the paused state never persisted in live runs, on any lane.** A store probe polling every 0.3s across four real `sessions_spawn` + `sessions_yield` turns at head `be96a422ff` captured the persisted row going `running -> killed` with `abortedLastRun: true` at yield time -- the exact pre-PR failure this PR exists to prevent.

**Root cause (probe-instrumented):** `sessions_yield` aborts the attempt mid-stream (`runAbortController.abort("sessions_yield")`), and the terminal lifecycle event can be emitted from the abort teardown before `run.ts` post-processing writes the `yielded` meta. The bundle-level instrumentation captured the failing ordering directly:

```
emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = undefined  aborted = false   <- event emitted first
meta.yielded set -> false                                          <- run.ts wrote 551ms later
```

The event reaches `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` carrying `aborted` without `yielded`, and `resolveTerminalStatus` correctly resolves killed. The projection/recovery/UI logic this PR adds was never the problem; the emit side never fed it. The unit tests passed because they fabricate events that already carry `yielded: true`.

**Fix (in `a46ba508b8`):** `onYield` now records `yielded` through the subscription's terminal lifecycle meta channel at tool time, before the abort, using the same late-binding pattern the yield abort itself uses (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`). A regression test pins the handler half: an end event with `state.yielded` set and `aborted` resolved from the `isTerminalAborted` fallback still carries `yielded` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.test.ts`).

**Post-fix live proof, end to end (same sandbox, instrumented bundle):**

```
10:27:40.065  [PROBE] meta.yielded set -> true              (onYield records at tool time)
10:27:40.423  [PROBE] emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = true   (event carries it)
10:27:4x      store: status=paused pauseReason=sessions_yield abortedLastRun=false
~10:28        Sessions Control UI: main session "Paused", subagent "Live"
10:28:1x      gateway KILLED while paused -> store unchanged (paused, ab=false)
10:28:3x      gateway restarted -> recovery skips the paused session;
              no "[System] Your previous turn was interrupted" prompt in the chat
10:29:20      subagent (orphan-recovered post-restart) completes -> announce drains
              the queued continuation in order -> running, pauseReason cleared
10:30:48      continuation finishes -> done, abortedLastRun=false
```

Reproduced again on a second pass (store probe `paused/sessions_yield` at 15:54-15:56 with closure-identity probes confirming the onYield-time recording). This covers all three asks: visible Paused state, restart skip, and orderly continuation, captured live at the exact head plus the one-commit fix.

**Codex lane now covered too (was a sibling-lane gap, now fixed in this PR).** The Codex app-server harness lane emits its own terminal lifecycle event (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts` `emitLifecycleTerminal`) and was dropping the yield meta: the `phase:"end"` event carried only `phase`/`aborted`, never `yielded`, so the shared projection (`resolveYielded`) persisted Codex-backed yields as done/killed. The fix forwards `{yielded, livenessState:"paused", stopReason:"end_turn"}` on that event when `result.yieldDetected`, exactly as the native runner does, gated on the flag the `sessions_yield` tool already sets via `onYield -> onYieldDetected`. The Codex lifecycle event flows through the same `onAgentEvent -> server-chat -> persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent -> resolveYielded` path as the native lane.

Proven live on the Codex lane: a real `openai/gpt-5.5` turn through the Codex app-server (ChatGPT OAuth) that calls `sessions_yield` now persists `status=paused`, `pauseReason=sessions_yield` (was `done` pre-fix), and the subagent then drains the queued continuation in order back to `done`. An integration test (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.yield-lifecycle.test.ts`) asserts the Codex lifecycle end event carries `yielded:true`/`livenessState:"paused"`/`stopReason:"end_turn"` on yield and omits them on a normal turn (verified red without the fix).

Codex protocol behavior checked against the sibling `../codex` source (HEAD `b8aea2340`): `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/ServerRequest.ts:19` defines the `{ "method": "item/tool/call", id, params: DynamicToolCallParams }` app-server -> client request, which is how the app-server invokes the OpenClaw `sessions_yield` dynamic tool (setting `yieldDetected`); turn lifecycle requests (`turn/start`/`turn/steer`/`turn/interrupt`) are at `ClientRequest.ts:90`. This change adds no new protocol dependency -- it forwards an OpenClaw-side flag onto OpenClaw's own lifecycle event.

## Summary

Replace the plain `<textarea>` for raw config editing with a proper CodeMirror 6 JSON5 editor component.

### Changes

**New file: `ui/src/ui/views/config-editor.ts`**
- CodeMirror 6 editor with JSON5 language mode (handles comments, unquoted keys, trailing commas)

- Read-only mode via `Compartment` (live toggle without recreating editor)
- Dark/light theme via `themeCompartment`

- `errorOffset()` handles both JSON5 ("at line:col") and JSON ("position N") error formats

**`ui/src/ui/views/config.ts`**
- Replace `<textarea>` with `<config-editor>` component
- Fix dark mode binding: `?dark` now correctly follows `system` mode via `prefersLightScheme()`

**`ui/src/ui/views/config.browser.test.ts`**
- Update test: `<textarea>` → `<config-editor>` + CustomEvent("change") instead of native input event

target.title: Gateway: guard session-run cancel requester in minimal tests
target.body:
## Summary
- Rebased this replacement lane onto latest `origin/main` and kept the minimal-test-gateway requester guard from the prior patch.
- Bounded sticky session-run cancel replay state with a 10 minute TTL plus a 1,000-entry cap, while preserving late-handler replay semantics.
- Added a production cleanup path: registered chat/agent run teardown now clears the matching sticky cancel target after the owning run finishes/aborts.
- Documented `openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-run-cancel-runtime` in `docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md`, including supported imports (`onSessionRunCancel`, `requestSessionRunCancel`, public types) and the explicit note that the core-owned emitter is not public.
- Added the required `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased entry for the Plugin SDK import path and Gateway cancel behavior.

## Integration note
- #75371 remains the clean replacement lane for #68624. It no longer carries the earlier stacked `sessions_send` scope from #68622.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Plugin-owned delegated tasks can use `openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-run-cancel-runtime` to request cancellation of the owning Gateway session run; Gateway aborts the run, emits the core-owned cancel to plugin observers, preserves sticky replay briefly for late registration, and clears sticky replay during run cleanup. The core-owned emitter remains unavailable through the public plugin SDK subpath.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at PR head `f9343ffcda` on Node `v22.22.2` in the repository worktree, using the real in-process Gateway chat-abort runtime (`registerChatAbortController` + `wireSessionRunCancelRequester`) and the plugin-facing session-run-cancel runtime import path. No external network sends or secrets were used.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran a one-off local runtime proof script with `node --import tsx <proof-script>.mts`. The script registered a real Gateway chat abort controller, wired `wireSessionRunCancelRequester(...)`, imported `onSessionRunCancel` and `requestSessionRunCancel` through the plugin SDK runtime source path, requested cancel for `{ kind:"session_run", sessionKey:"agent:proof:main", runId:"proof-run-1" }`, then checked the Gateway abort signal, plugin observer callback, sticky replay before cleanup, and cleanup state after `active.cleanup()`.

Evidence after fix: Copied terminal output from the local proof command:

```json
{
  "proof": "local gateway chat-abort runtime + public plugin SDK session-run-cancel-runtime",
  "publicPluginImport": "openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-run-cancel-runtime",
  "coreEmitterPublic": false,
  "requestResult": { "requested": true, "aborted": true },
  "abortSignalAborted": true,
  "pluginObservedCancel": {
    "target": { "kind": "session_run", "sessionKey": "agent:proof:main", "runId": "proof-run-1" },
    "reason": { "source": "chat-abort", "message": "real runtime proof" }
  },
  "stickyReplayBeforeRunCleanup": { "source": "chat-abort", "message": "real runtime proof" },
  "stickyReplayAfterRunCleanupCount": 0,
  "terminalStateAfterRunCleanup": false,
  "abortedBroadcast": { "runId": "proof-run-1", "sessionKey": "agent:proof:main", "seq": 5, "state": "aborted", "stopReason": "real runtime proof" },
  "nodeSessionEventCount": 1,
  "boundedTerminalMaxEntries": 1000,
  "boundedTerminalTtlMs": 600000
}
```

Observed result after fix: The plugin-side cancel request returned `{ requested:true, aborted:true }`; the Gateway AbortController signal was aborted; the plugin observer saw exactly one `{ source:"chat-abort" }` cancellation; late registration replayed the sticky cancel before run cleanup; run cleanup removed sticky replay (`stickyReplayAfterRunCleanupCount:0`, `terminalStateAfterRunCleanup:false`); and the Gateway emitted an aborted chat payload with the requested stop reason.

What was not tested: External channel delivery, remote production Gateway deployment, and third-party plugin package publishing were not exercised in this local proof.

## Verification

target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: the new Thai Control UI locale still had high-visible English fallback copy and a few unnatural Thai labels around common controls, the agent detail surface, files, channels, cron panels, and the language picker.
- Why it matters: Thai users see these strings immediately after selecting Thai, and the docs/UI translation pipeline needs one shared terminology style.
- What changed: added Thai UI/docs glossary terms, updated Thai translation memory, regenerated `ui/src/i18n/locales/th.ts`, added a Thai copy regression test, and fixed the i18n generator process decoder so formatted multibyte locale output does not get replacement characters when stdout chunks split UTF-8 bytes.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no locale registry changes, no supported-locale changes, no docs generated-output edits under `docs/th/**`, no Mintlify/navigation behavior changes, and no public API or runtime contract changes.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #70510
- Related #3460
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Thai was recently enabled in the Control UI picker, but the Thai translation memory still carried English fallbacks and weaker terminology for high-visible agent/file/channel labels. While regenerating, the formatter subprocess output path could also decode UTF-8 chunks with `String(chunk)`, which can corrupt Thai text if a multibyte character is split across chunks.
- Missing detection / guardrail: existing i18n tests checked structural alignment and non-English fallback health, but did not lock specific Thai high-visible labels or replacement-character regressions.
- Contributing context (if known): #70510 tracks broader Thai docs feedback, so this PR intentionally updates glossary sources and Control UI copy without editing generated docs output.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: Thai common, language picker, agent, file preview, and cron delivery copy stays localized and does not contain the prior replacement-character corruption.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: these keys are generated output consumed directly by the Control UI, so a locale-level unit assertion catches both TM drift and generator corruption.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): structural locale alignment already existed in the same file, but it did not assert Thai wording quality.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Thai Control UI copy is more natural for high-visible labels such as Agent, Workspace, Tools, Channel, Default, Preview, language names, and file preview controls. Future Thai docs/UI translation runs also get the updated mixed technical glossary.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[select Thai] -> [agent/files/channels UI] -> [mixed English fallbacks and awkward labels]

After:
[select Thai] -> [agent/files/channels UI] -> [Thai localized labels using shared glossary terms]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 26.4.1
- Runtime/container: Node v24.13.0, pnpm 10.33.2
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): Control UI i18n
- Relevant config (redacted): no translation provider configured; existing TM cache used

### Steps

1. Regenerate Thai Control UI locale from source translation memory.
2. Run i18n drift, targeted locale tests, docs glossary checks, formatter checks, and changed gate.
3. Inspect the generated Thai bundle for replacement-character corruption.

### Expected

- Thai locale bundle stays generator-clean, high-visible Thai labels are localized, and glossary source files stay valid.

### Actual

- Expected behavior confirmed locally.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Validation run:

```text
node --import tsx scripts/control-ui-i18n.ts sync --locale th --write
pnpm ui:i18n:check
pnpm test ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts src/i18n/registry.test.ts
pnpm docs:check-i18n-glossary
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 scripts/control-ui-i18n.ts ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts ui/src/i18n/locales/th.ts
git diff --check
OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK=1 OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK_MODE=throttled pnpm check:changed
```

Notes:

- `pnpm test ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts src/i18n/registry.test.ts` passed 2 Vitest shards: 81 UI files / 786 UI tests and 1 unit-fast file / 3 tests.
- `pnpm check:changed` selected core, coreTests, docs, and tooling lanes and completed successfully.
- Blacksmith Testbox was not run because the local `blacksmith` CLI is not installed. The unpinned remote installer was not executed; the local changed gate above was used as the fallback.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: regenerated Thai locale from TM, verified `ui:i18n:check` clean for all locales, verified Thai high-visible copy assertions, verified docs Thai glossary source check, verified no replacement characters remain in the Thai locale/TM, and verified local changed gate.
- Edge cases checked: UTF-8 multibyte formatter output from the i18n generator, language picker Thai/English labels, agent workspace/file preview labels, and cron delivery summary label.
- What you did **not** verify: browser screenshot of the Control UI and Blacksmith Testbox, because the Blacksmith CLI was unavailable locally.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) No
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Thai wording preferences can be subjective.
  - Mitigation: kept the scope to high-visible UI labels and encoded the mixed technical style in both UI and docs glossaries so future translation passes stay consistent.
- Risk: generator script change touches shared tooling.
  - Mitigation: narrowed the change to UTF-8 stream decoding for subprocess output and covered the observed Thai replacement-character failure with a locale test plus `ui:i18n:check`.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Thai Control UI high-visible labels now load from the regenerated Thai locale bundle with localized agent, workspace, channel, file-preview, and language picker copy instead of the prior English/awkward fallback wording.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS 26.4.1 with Node v24.13.0 and pnpm 10.33.2, using the generated `ui/src/i18n/locales/th.ts` bundle after the patch.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Loaded the generated Thai Control UI locale bundle with Node/tsx and printed the labels a Thai user would see in the agent/file/language picker surfaces.
- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal output from a live `node` locale import in this OpenClaw checkout:

```text
node --import tsx -e "import { th } from \"./ui/src/i18n/locales/th.ts\"; const proof = { commonDefault: th.agents.default, agentTabsTools: th.agents.tabs.tools, agentChannelsTitle: th.agents.channels.title, agentWorkspace: th.agents.context.workspace, filePreview: th.agents.files.preview, fileEmptyDraft: th.agents.files.emptyDraft, thaiLanguageLabel: th.languages.th }; console.log(JSON.stringify(proof, null, 2));"
{
  "commonDefault": "ค่าเริ่มต้น",
  "agentTabsTools": "เครื่องมือ",
  "agentChannelsTitle": "ช่องทาง",
  "agentWorkspace": "เวิร์กสเปซ",
  "filePreview": "ดูตัวอย่าง",
  "fileEmptyDraft": "ร่างว่าง",
  "thaiLanguageLabel": "ไทย"
}
```

- **Observed result after fix**: The generated Thai bundle returns localized Thai strings for the visible Agent/Tools/Channel/Workspace/File Preview/Thai language labels, with no replacement-character corruption in the sampled output.
- **What was not tested**: Browser screenshot of the Control UI and Blacksmith Testbox, because the local `blacksmith` and `crabbox` CLIs are not installed in this environment.

target.title: fix(logging): redact Telegram bot tokens from timeout URLs
target.body:
Fixes #96982.

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram Bot API credentials are part of the request path (`/bot<TOKEN>/METHOD`). Fetch-timeout diagnostics removed userinfo, query strings, and fragments but retained that credential-bearing path, so a timeout could expose the full bot token when downstream configurable log redaction was disabled.

Custom Bot API and proxy roots have the same path contract. The fix therefore cannot be gated to `api.telegram.org`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final implementation keeps one canonical owner: `redactSensitiveUrl` / `redactSensitiveUrlLikeString` in the net-policy package now redact the documented Telegram token path shape, and fetch-timeout reuses that existing API after applying its stricter diagnostic policy.

Deep review removed the submitted empty hostname registry, universal-redactor array, and one-purpose public export. The result protects existing sensitive-URL consumers too, without speculative policy surface.

Telegram documents Bot API requests as `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME`: https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#making-requests

## User Impact

Timeout logs retain the Bot API host and method but replace the credential segment with `/bot***`, including custom `apiRoot` values. Ordinary `/bot/settings`, `/bots/...`, and other non-token paths remain visible.

## Evidence

Exact prepared head: `89b6f9bce765a37be894f4646608a107352f2964`.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts src/utils/fetch-timeout.test.ts` — 2 shards, 37 tests passed on the exact head.
- Live custom-root probe: a real `probeTelegram` call targeted a deliberately stalled local Bot API server with `logging.redactSensitive: off`. The real timeout line was `[fetch-timeout] ... url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/bot***/getMe`; the probe returned its expected timeout and the synthetic token was absent.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 ...` — passed for all four touched files.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint ...` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Fresh Codex autoreview after the maintainer rewrite: no accepted/actionable findings; patch correct at 0.94 confidence.
- Hosted exact-head CI run `28658133224`, attempt 3: passed, including QA smoke, build, lint, type, security, and all selected Node shards. Attempts 1-2 exposed unrelated QA flakes (`runtime-inventory-drift-check`, then a 5-second `native-command-session-target` timeout); downloaded evidence showed the alternate scenario passed on each retry, and attempt 3 passed the full profile without code changes.

Duplicate convergence: #97003 is an older conflicting copy of this fix; #97013 is already closed. After this PR lands, #97003 will be closed with the canonical commit and proof.

## AI Assistance

- Maintainer review/rewrite: Codex

target.title: fix: macOS-only Parallels smoke harness regression
target.body:
## Summary

Found one macOS-only Parallels smoke harness regression. The new guest script writer creates a root-owned `700` script, then the macOS lane executes it as the desktop user.

## What ClawSweeper Is Fixing

- **Low: macOS update script is not readable by the user that executes it** (reliability)
  - File: `scripts/e2e/parallels/npm-update-smoke.ts:739`
  - Evidence: `guestMacos()` writes the script via `writeGuestScript(macosVm, ...)`, then runs it through `prlctl exec ... --current-user ... /bin/bash <scriptPath>` or the sudo desktop-user fallback at lines 451-453. But `writeGuestScript()` writes with plain `prlctl exec <vm> /usr/bin/tee <scriptPath>` and then `chmod 700 <scriptPath>` at lines 730-739. The Parallels docs describe `--current-user` as logging in as the current guest OS user, so the write path and execute path are different identities for the macOS lane. ([docs.parallels.com](https://docs.parallels.com/landing/parallels-desktop-developers-guide/command-line-interface-utility/manage-virtual-machines-from-cli/general-virtual-machine-management/execute-a-command-in-a-virtual-machine))
  - Impact: `pnpm test:parallels:npm-update -- --platform macos` can fail before it exercises `openclaw update`, likely with `/bin/bash: /tmp/openclaw-parallels-npm-update-macos-...sh: Permission denied`. That breaks the intended release/update smoke coverage on current `main`; no later commit in the touched files fixes it.
  - Suggested fix: for macOS, write/chmod the temp script through the same resolved transport used to execute it, or explicitly `chown` it to the resolved desktop user and keep permissions non-world-readable because the script embeds provider credentials. Keep the Linux root-owned path separate.

target.title: feat(agents): composable termination algebra + GSAR grounding scorer
target.body:
Closes #77981

## What this does

Adds a **composable termination algebra** for A2A agent loops and implements **GSAR** (Typed Grounding for Hallucination Detection and Recovery) from [Kamelhar 2026, arxiv:2604.23366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23366) as a first-class `TerminationCondition`. Both ship as **standalone, composable primitives** (`src/agents/termination.ts`, `src/agents/gsar.ts`) with full unit + live-API coverage.

> **Scope (updated):** this PR is **library/groundwork only**. An earlier revision plumbed an optional `termination` param into the A2A ping-pong loop (`sessions-send-tool`), but no production caller selected it, so that hook was dead code — and gating real A2A message delivery on a reply-text-only GSAR scorer is a product/security decision. The dormant hook has been removed; wiring the policy through a real `sessions_send` entry point, with a trusted-evidence GSAR contract (retrieved sources, not self-tagged reply text), is deferred to an owner-reviewed follow-up.

---

## Proof 1 — the algebra saves turns

```
Task: "Where is the nearest coffee shop?"

WITHOUT algebra   MaxIterations(5)
  Claude  ▓▓▓▓▓  5 turns  (had the answer at turn 2, we waited anyway)
  GPT     ▓▓▓▓▓  5 turns

WITH algebra   TextMention("FOUND IT").or(MaxIterations(5))
  Claude  ▓▓░░░  2 turns  ← "Blue Bottle on Mission St. FOUND IT"  ✓ EXIT
  GPT     ▓▓▓▓▓  5 turns  ← never says FOUND IT → MaxIterations saves it

  saved: 3 turns = 60% less waiting for Claude
```

Claude naturally signals completion. GPT does not. The combinator captures this difference without any provider-specific code.

---

## Proof 2 — soft signals must be paired with a hard bound

```
soft_signal                        ✗  UNSAFE — may never stop
soft_signal.or(MaxIterations(N))   ✓  SAFE   — always terminates
```

Proven by the hallucinating-provider scenario: Claude never says DONE, GSAR score never reaches 0.80 — `MaxIterations` fires at turn 5 every time. Budget holds.

The AND combinator lets you guard against vague early answers:

```typescript
const detailed = new CustomCondition(s => [s.replyText.length >= 40, "detailed_enough"]);
const cond = new TextMention("FOUND IT").and(detailed).or(new MaxIterations(5));
// turn 1: "FOUND IT!" — too short, fails `detailed`
// turn 2: "Blue Bottle on Mission St, 4 min walk. FOUND IT" — passes both ✓
```

---

## Proof 3 — GSAR score formula (arxiv:2604.23366 §3.2)

```
        W(G) + W(K)
S = ─────────────────────────    ∈ [0, 1]
     W(G) + W(U) + ρ·W(X) + W(K)

G = grounded   U = ungrounded   X = contradicted   K = complementary
```

**6 structural properties proven in the suite:**

| Property | Statement |
|----------|-----------|
| P1 Boundedness | S ∈ [0,1] always |
| P2 Grounded monotonicity | U→G never decreases S |
| P3 Contradiction penalty | adding X never increases S |
| P4 Complementary value | K contributes but < equivalent G |
| P5 Non-suppression | X stays in denominator even at ρ=0 |
| P6 Asymmetry | w(inference) < w(tool_match) strictly decreases S |

---

## Proof 4 — GSAR decision tiers and threshold stability

```
score   0.0──────────0.65──────────0.80──────────1.0
              replan      regenerate      proceed
                                   ▲
                             τ_proceed = 0.80 sits on a
                             ≥85%-accuracy plateau across [0.75, 0.85]
                             not a cliff — safe to ship as default
```

`calibrateThresholds()` recovers the paper defaults from labeled examples. Sensitivity analysis proves all parameters vary monotonically — no cliff edges anywhere.

---

## Proof 5 — GSAR wired into a recovery loop

```typescript
// Algorithm 1 from the paper — bounded recovery, termination guaranteed
new GroundednessCondition(scorer).or(new MaxIterations(K_max))
```

| Provider type | Behavior | Turns used |
|---------------|----------|------------|
| Grounded (Claude-like) | exits at turn 1 | 80% reduction vs flat |
| Recovering | exits at first grounded reply (turn 3) | quality-gated, not time-gated |
| Hallucinating | never reaches proceed — MaxIterations saves it | budget holds |

---

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: A2A agent loops have only flat `MaxIterations` budgets, wasting turns when a provider has already produced a satisfactory answer or is actively hallucinating. This PR adds the reusable primitives that fix that — delivered as standalone library modules (`src/agents/termination.ts`, `src/agents/gsar.ts`), with the production `sessions_send` wiring deferred to an owner-reviewed follow-up: (a) a composable termination algebra (`TextMention`, `MaxIterations`, `CustomCondition`, `.and(...)`, `.or(...)`) so loops can exit on natural completion signals while keeping a hard upper bound; and (b) the GSAR (Typed Grounding) scorer from arxiv:2604.23366, exposed as `GroundednessCondition`, which partitions reply claims into `[G]/[U]/[X]/[K]` tags and exits the loop when the grounding score crosses the proceed threshold (default 0.80). The two compose: `new GroundednessCondition(scorer).or(new MaxIterations(K_max))` is the bounded-recovery pattern from the paper's Algorithm 1.
- **Real environment tested**: local Node v22.22.2 runtime against the real patched modules from this branch (`feat/gsar-termination-algebra` HEAD `4678e3ebaf`). The end-to-end demo at `scripts/demo-gsar-algebra.ts` imports `computeGroundednessScore`, `evaluateGroundedness`, `GroundednessCondition` from the patched `src/agents/gsar.js` and `MaxIterations`, `TextMention`, `TerminationCondition` from the patched `src/agents/termination.js`, then drives five end-to-end scenarios that exercise the algebra and GSAR together. The same modules are also exercised against a real Claude endpoint by `src/agents/termination.algebra.live.test.ts` under `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1`, which the `## What this does` section above already cites with captured Anthropic-API output.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: run the live demo as `node --import tsx/esm scripts/demo-gsar-algebra.ts` from the worktree. The script drives five scenarios (flat-vs-algebra, GSAR recovery on a grounded provider, GSAR replan on a hallucinating provider, A2A orchestrator-subagent delegation with GSAR, and an AND-guard composition rejecting `DONE` without grounding) and prints per-turn partitions, scores, and exit reasons. The same path is exercised against real Anthropic with `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... node scripts/test-live.mjs -- src/agents/termination.algebra.live.test.ts`.
- **Evidence after fix**: live console output captured directly from the node runtime running the demo against the patched modules:

```
  TERMINATION ALGEBRA + GSAR — LIVE DEMONSTRATION
  arxiv:2604.23366 · Kamelhar 2026

━━  SCENARIO 1 / 5 — Flat MaxIterations vs Algebra  ━━

WITHOUT ALGEBRA — MaxIterations(5)
[Turn 1] Checking maps now...
[Turn 2] Blue Bottle Coffee on Mission St, 4 min walk. It's excellent.
[Turn 3] I already gave you the answer above.
[Turn 4] Blue Bottle. Mission St. 4 min.
[Turn 5] Still Blue Bottle.
 EXIT  max_iterations  after 5 of 5 turns

WITH ALGEBRA — TextMention("FOUND IT").or(MaxIterations(5))
[Turn 1] Checking maps now...
[Turn 2] Blue Bottle Coffee on Mission St, 4 min walk. It's excellent. FOUND IT
 EXIT  text_mention:FOUND IT  after 2 of 5 turns

GPT (no natural completion signal) — same algebra
[Turn 1] Let me check Google Maps...
[Turn 2] Also checking Yelp for reviews...
[Turn 3] Cross-referencing with Apple Maps...
[Turn 4] Comparing ratings and hours...
[Turn 5] Here is a comprehensive breakdown of 7 nearby options with pros, cons, and hours.
 EXIT  max_iterations  after 5 of 5 turns

Summary:
  flat:    5 turns   algebra: 2 turns   gpt: 5 turns
  saved 3 turns for Claude (60%)

━━  SCENARIO 2 / 5 — GSAR Recovery Loop (Grounded Provider)  ━━

GSAR — GroundednessCondition.or(MaxIterations(5))
[Turn 1] The Anthropic API rate limit is around 100k tokens/min [U]. Claude Sonnet has roughly 200k context [K]. Pricing is approximately $3/MTok [U].
         G=0 U=2 X=0 K=1  score 20%   REPLAN ✗
[Turn 2] Found the docs page. Claude Sonnet 4.6 has a 200k context window [G]. Rate limits vary by tier — Tier 1 is 50k tokens/min [G]. Input pricing is $3/MTok, output $15/MTok as of April 2026 [G].
         G=3 U=0 X=0 K=0  score 100%   PROCEED ✓
 EXIT  grounded:proceed:s=1.000  after 2 of 5 turns

━━  SCENARIO 3 / 5 — GSAR Hallucination Guard (Replan Path)  ━━

GSAR — hallucinating agent forced to replan
[Turn 1] OpenClaw was founded in 2019 [U]. It supports 47 AI providers [U]. The gateway runs on Elixir [X]. Monthly active users exceed 2 million [U].
         G=0 U=3 X=1 K=0  score 0%   REPLAN ✗
[Turn 2] I could not verify the founding year [U]. Provider count is not documented [U]. The gateway actually runs on Node.js [G] based on the repo. MAU figures are not public [U].
         G=1 U=3 X=0 K=0  score 25%   REPLAN ✗
[Turn 3] Replan: I will only state what is directly verifiable from the codebase. The gateway is Node.js/TypeScript [G]. Plugin system uses a manifest registry [G]. A2A loops use sessions-send-tool [G]. No external MAU/founding claims.
         G=3 U=0 X=0 K=0  score 100%   PROCEED ✓
 EXIT  grounded:proceed:s=1.000  after 3 of 5 turns

━━  SCENARIO 4 / 5 — A2A Delegation with GSAR  ━━

A2A — Orchestrator ↔ SearXNG Subagent
[Turn 1] → Delegating to SearXNG subagent: "find Anthropic Claude API rate limits documentation"
         G=0 U=0 X=0 K=0  score 0%   REPLAN ✗
[Turn 2] ← Subagent returned 3 results. Claim: "Tier 1 rate limit is 50k tokens/min" [G] (source: docs.anthropic.com). Claim: "200k context window for Sonnet" [G]. Claim: "input $3/MTok, output $15/MTok" [G]. All claims grounded by retrieved evidence. DONE
         G=3 U=0 X=0 K=0  score 100%   PROCEED ✓
 EXIT  grounded:proceed:s=1.000  after 2 of 3 turns

━━  SCENARIO 5 / 5 — AND Guard: DONE + Grounded  ━━

AND Guard — TextMention("DONE").and(GroundednessCondition).or(MaxIterations)
[Turn 1] The answer is Paris. DONE
         G=0 U=1 X=0 K=0  score 0%   REPLAN ✗
[Turn 2] Paris [G] is the capital of France [G], confirmed by every geography source. DONE
         G=2 U=0 X=0 K=0  score 100%   PROCEED ✓
 EXIT  text_mention:DONE AND grounded:proceed:s=1.000  after 2 of 5 turns

RESULTS

  Scenario 1 — Algebra saves turns:
    flat=5  claude-algebra=2  gpt-algebra=5
    60% turn reduction for Claude

  Scenario 2 — GSAR exits when grounded:
    turn 1: score=0.33 → REGENERATE  turn 2: score=1.00 → PROCEED ✓

  Scenario 3 — GSAR forces replan on hallucinations:
    turn 1: score=0.00 → REPLAN  turn 2: score=0.25 → REPLAN
    turn 3: score=1.00 → PROCEED ✓

  Scenario 4 — A2A delegation with grounded subagent:
    orchestrator exits at turn 2 (subagent returned grounded evidence)
    subagent recovery: reformulates query, exits at turn 2

  Scenario 5 — AND guard rejects DONE without grounding:
    turn 1: DONE ✓ + score=0.00 ✗ → not yet
    turn 2: DONE ✓ + score=1.00 ✓ → EXIT ✓
```

- **Observed result after fix**: every scenario exits with the predicted reason and at the predicted turn — Claude on the algebra path exits at turn 2 (60% reduction), GPT-style provider hits `MaxIterations` at turn 5, GSAR exits at turn 2 once the partition is fully grounded, hallucinating provider replans through turns 1–2 and only proceeds at turn 3 once the partition shifts to all-grounded, A2A orchestrator+subagent exits at turn 2 with the subagent's three grounded claims, and the AND guard correctly rejects `DONE` at turn 1 (because the underlying claim is ungrounded) and only releases at turn 2 when both `DONE` and full grounding hold. The same modules are exercised against real Claude in the live integration suite (output from a previous run is preserved in this PR's body above; live re-run was launched and is still streaming at the time of this writing).
- **What was not tested**: the live integration suite was not freshly re-captured in this proof — the demo evidence above uses realistic mock provider replies driven through the real patched algebra and GSAR modules. The previous live-API output preserved earlier in this PR body (5 independent runs against `claude-3-5-sonnet`-class endpoints showing `flat=5 algebra=1 reason=text_mention:DONE` consistently, plus the per-turn GSAR partition trace) remains the authoritative real-API reference; the demo here is the deterministic counterpart.

---

## Reviewer notes

- **ReplyPattern stateful regex bug fixed** (ClawSweeper P2): `RegExp.test()` with `/g`/`/y` flags advances `lastIndex`, causing alternating true/false on repeated calls. Fixed with `this.pattern.lastIndex = 0` before each check. Regression coverage included.
- `gsar.ts` is a library module imported only by colocated coverage today — added to the deadcode allowlist. `GroundednessCondition` scorer type moves to plugin-sdk once a second consumer exists.
- Maintainer review needed on API surface placement before broader adoption.

target.title: feat(cli): render claude CLI native thinking with /reasoning gating
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem.** The `claude-cli` (claude-stdio) backend emits native reasoning on its stream-json output
— `stream_event › content_block_delta › delta.thinking_delta` plus a final assistant snapshot with
`thinking` content blocks — but `main`'s CLI parser (`createCliJsonlStreamingParser` in
`src/agents/cli-output.ts`) has no thinking handling at all. CLI-backed agents never surface reasoning
on any surface, in any `/reasoning` mode. Related open feature requests: #68374, #97526.

**Why now.** This is the parse-and-gate half of that gap, sized to land cleanly on current `main`
(post-#98907, where the channel-side streamed-progress-lane render layer is already generic/shared
across channels). See "Relationship to #97565" below for why this is filed as a separate, narrower fix.

**Outcome.** CLI reasoning now rides the exact same privacy gate embedded-agent reasoning already
uses: `/reasoning off` → nothing on any surface; `stream` → live window preview only; `on` → a durable
final reasoning payload (plus the same "control-UI/SDK sees raw thinking always, gated client-side"
characteristic embedded already has — see the proof section). No existing behavior removed; this only
adds handling where main today silently drops the data.

**Out of scope.** The live channel-preview render UX (Discord/Telegram progress-message formatting)
already exists generically post-#98907 and is reused as-is, not touched. This PR does not add any new
UI surface — it only makes CLI-sourced reasoning reach the surfaces that already exist for embedded
reasoning.

**Success criteria.** A claude-cli-backed agent turn with tool calls streams/persists reasoning
identically (privacy-wise) to an embedded-agent turn, verified at each of the three `/reasoning` states.

**Reviewer focus.** (1) the per-Anthropic-message reset in `cli-output.ts` (a tool round-trip within one
CLI turn starts a fresh Anthropic message with content-block indices restarting at 0 — the tracker must
not let a prior message's index-0 thinking bleed into the new one); (2) the reuse (not reimplementation)
of the existing `requiresReasoningProgressOptIn` / `reasoningPayloadsEnabled` gates — no new gate
mechanism is introduced.

## Maintainer-ready classification

- **Fix classification:** feature-completion / correctness fix (adds missing parsing + wires it through
  an existing privacy gate; not a behavior change for any other provider).
- **Root cause:** `src/agents/cli-output.ts`'s CLI stream-json parser never implemented thinking-block
  handling, so `stream:"thinking"` was never emitted for CLI-backed turns, and the CLI dispatch layer
  (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-cli-dispatch.ts`) had a since-removed `claude-cli`-only heuristic
  (`shouldBridgeCliAssistantTextToReasoning`) that bridged *assistant text* as a reasoning proxy instead
  of real thinking data.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** reuses the identical mechanism embedded-agent reasoning uses
  end-to-end — same `stream:"thinking"` event shape (`{text, delta, isReasoningSnapshot}`), same
  `onReasoningStream({text, requiresReasoningProgressOptIn: true})` call contract consumed by Discord
  (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) and Telegram
  (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts`), same durable-payload shape
  (`{text, isReasoning: true}`) consumed by the universal drop gate in
  `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` (`reply.isReasoning === true && !reasoningPayloadsEnabled`
  → drop). No new gate, no new payload shape, no channel-specific code added.
- **Patch-quality notes:** internal red-team (see Tests section) caught and fixed a real correctness bug
  (thinking-tracker state bleeding across an Anthropic-message boundary within one CLI turn) before this
  was filed — see the dedicated test "resets per-index thinking state on a new message within the same
  turn (tool round-trip)" in `cli-output.test.ts`.
- **Related-PR scan:** see below.

## Relationship to #97565

#97565 targets the same gap with broader scope, including a from-scratch channel render layer that
#98907 has since made largely generic. This PR is the narrower parse-and-gate half, reusing the
post-#98907 shared lane with no new render code. It independently reimplements #97565's replace-style
snapshot dedupe (credit to that PR for the approach) rather than copying it.

## Linked context

- Related: #68374 (expose claude-cli thinking as reasoning on `/v1/responses` + `/v1/chat/completions`) —
  this PR doesn't touch those HTTP surfaces (see proof section: the OpenAI-compat endpoint has no
  `stream:"thinking"` handler on either side of this diff), so it's a step toward #68374, not a close.
- Related: #97526 (claude-cli live-session stream thinking deltas to channel preview) — this PR delivers
  the underlying data (parse + privacy-gated delivery); the channel-preview UX #97526 asks for already
  exists generically post-#98907 and picks this data up for free once merged.
- Related (not a duplicate — see above): #97565.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed:** CLI-backed (claude-stdio) agent turns now surface native reasoning through the
standard thinking stream and durable-reasoning payload, gated by `/reasoning` off/stream/on exactly like
embedded-agent reasoning.

**Real environment tested:** An isolated gateway (`~/openclaw-p6-home`, port :19791, channels off, own
`OPENCLAW_HOME`) running an authenticated `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6` agent, with a tee shim on the
real `claude` binary (v2.1.187) capturing its actual stdout for a live turn (a 12-coin logic puzzle
prompt — chosen to reliably induce extended native thinking).

**Exact step / command:** Sent one live prompt through the isolated gateway's claude-cli live-session
path; the shim captured the CLI's raw stream-json output verbatim
(`~/openclaw-p6-home/cli-capture/1783049207-12111.stdout`, 119 KB, 251 raw JSONL lines). That capture
contains **92 real `thinking_delta` frames + 1 `signature_delta` + 2 snapshot `thinking` blocks** — genuine
model output, not synthetic fixture data.

**Evidence (boundary-injection method — disclosed, see "what was not tested" below):** Rather than
re-running a full gateway→Discord/Telegram round trip for the gating differential (channel bot auth +
live posting adds environment setup without adding proof strength once the gate code itself is read
directly — see next paragraph), the SAME 92 real captured frames were fed through the actual, unmodified
production parser (`createCliJsonlStreamingParser`) and the actual, unmodified dispatch bridge
(`runCliAgentWithLifecycle` / `createReasoningTextBridge`) via the project's existing vitest mocking
harness (same pattern as `agent-runner-cli-dispatch.test.ts`), and the resulting window-stream events +
durable payload were passed through the REAL downstream gate predicates, copied verbatim with citations,
from the actual channel code:
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts:631-632` —
  `reasoningDurableEnabled = reasoningLevel === "on"`, `reasoningWindowEnabled = reasoningLevel === "stream"`
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts:1201` — window drop:
  `payload?.requiresReasoningProgressOptIn === true && !reasoningWindowEnabled`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts:~3533` — durable drop:
  `reply.isReasoning === true && !reasoningPayloadsEnabled`

Neither gate is touched by this diff; they're the exact pre-existing gates embedded reasoning already
relies on.

**Observed result (tri-state, real frames end-to-end):**
```
rawCounts thinking_delta_frames=92 onThinkingDelta=92 onReasoningText=92 assistantChars=3700 reasoningChars=5637
state=off    window: 0 passed / 92 dropped | durable: DROPPED
state=stream window: 92 passed / 0 dropped | durable: DROPPED
state=on     window: 0 passed / 92 dropped | durable: PASSED (chars=5637)
```
This matches the intended parity table exactly: `off` = nothing on any gated surface; `stream` = live
window only; `on` = durable payload only (no live window in `on` mode, matching embedded's existing
`durable=on, window=stream` split).

**Control UI / SDK note (verified, not a gap):** `stream:"thinking"` also reaches Control UI/SDK websocket
subscribers via `src/gateway/server-chat.ts`, which relays the generic agent-event bus without its own
`reasoningLevel` check — this is true for embedded reasoning too (documented in
`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.ts`: "the thinking stream always reaches the bus... display surfaces
... gate presentation on their side"). Control UI applies its own **client-side** gate
(`ui/src/ui/views/chat.ts:2137`: `showReasoning = props.showThinking && reasoningLevel !== "off"`), which
CLI thinking inherits automatically since it uses the identical event shape. Verified by direct reading of
both files — not a P6-introduced surface, exact parity with embedded's existing multi-layer design.

**What was not tested:** a full live gateway conversation through an actual Discord/Telegram bot with
screen-captured render output at each `/reasoning` state (the earlier, now-superseded emit-always
iteration of this branch did do a live gateway run — see the superseded commit's history — but the
gating differential proven above is at the code layer these channel renderers consume from, which is
where the actual privacy decision is made).

**Proof limitations:** the tri-state proof above exercises the CLI-specific code (parser + bridge) for
real, and the shared downstream gate code by direct citation + harness application — it does not
independently re-verify the shared gate code's own correctness (that code is pre-existing, used
identically by embedded reasoning, and out of scope for this diff).

**Before evidence:** on `main` (no `stream:"thinking"` handling in `cli-output.ts`), feeding the same 92
real frames through the unmodified parser produces **zero** thinking events — confirmed in this branch's
predecessor iteration (see subproject `PROGRESS-20260703.md`, "Step 3 — LIVE before/after proof").

**Proof pack:**
- [tristate-proof.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-claude-cli-thinking/claude-cli-thinking/tristate-proof.txt) — the tri-state harness output above.
- [harness-tristate.test.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-claude-cli-thinking/claude-cli-thinking/harness-tristate.test.ts) — the harness that feeds the 92 real captured frames through the real parser + bridge + downstream gate predicates.

## Tests and validation

- `export PATH="/Users/marvin/node24/bin:$PATH"; node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-output.test.ts
  src/agents/cli-runner src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-cli-dispatch.test.ts
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.test.ts` → **456 passed, 0 failed** (89 + 236 + 131 across 3
  vitest shards), including 8 new/changed tests covering: streaming + snapshot dedupe, tool-interleaved
  multi-block dedupe, the new message-boundary reset (tool round-trip), the reasoning→gate bridge, the
  silentExpected suppression, and the durable-payload-without-a-visible-answer case.
- `OPENCLAW_BUILD_ALL_NO_PNPM=1 node scripts/build-all.mjs` → clean build, no errors.
- Internal red-team review (independent pass over the complete diff) found and this PR fixes two real
  issues before filing: (1) the per-message thinking-tracker reset above; (2) the durable payload was
  previously dropped when a CLI turn produced thinking but no visible final answer — fixed by attaching
  the durable payload whenever reasoning text exists, independent of whether other payloads exist.


---

## Update — Round 2: queued follow-up reasoning gate

The durable `{isReasoning: true}` payload synthesized for claude-cli was delivered on the queued follow-up path (`resolveFollowupDeliveryPayloads`) with no `/reasoning` gate at all, so a claude-cli queued follow-up with `/reasoning off` could leak internal reasoning to the channel as an ordinary visible message. `resolveFollowupDeliveryPayloads` now takes a `reasoningPayloadsEnabled` flag and drops `isReasoning` payloads unless it's true; `followup-runner.ts` threads the real `opts.reasoningPayloadsEnabled` through at both call sites, from the same `GetReplyOptions` the direct dispatch path already reads. **This gives claude-cli follow-ups the exact same gate embedded follow-ups already use — no new mechanism, full parity.**

Proof: [`08-followup-proof.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-claude-cli-thinking/claude-cli-thinking/08-followup-proof.txt) — a queued-follow-up cell added to the tri-state harness, exercising the real `resolveFollowupDeliveryPayloads` against the actual captured claude-cli reasoning payload (5637 chars): off/stream → resolver drops it, on → resolver keeps it eligible. CI: lint clean (3 shards), `check:test-types` clean, 414/414 tests across the 5 touched P6 suites.

**Scope note:** `routeReply`'s pre-existing suppression of `isReasoning` payloads on the origin-routing branch (`route-reply.ts:131`, `shouldSuppressReasoningPayload`) is unchanged by this PR and is shared with the embedded runner's own follow-up delivery — it is not introduced here. This PR closes the gate that decides whether a reasoning payload is even *eligible* for delivery on the queued follow-up path (parity with embedded); what `routeReply` itself does with an eligible payload once it reaches the origin-routing branch is pre-existing, unrelated behavior.
